parties:
Tusta Chandra Mandal  Plaintiff-Appellant-------- Petitioner
vs
Samsul Haque being dead his legal heirs-Nur Mohammad and others Defendant -Respondent------Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued, calling upon the opposite parties, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 10-4-2014 (decree signed on 15-4-2014), passed by the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No.135 of 2004, dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 10-4-2004 (decree signed on 17-4-2004), passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Savar, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.36 of 2002, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that one Sree Tusta Chandra Mandal son of late Rakhal Chandra Mandal, as plaintiff, had filed Title Suit No.36 of 2002, on 6-1-2002, before the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Savar, Dhaka, against Shamsul Haque and others, with a prayer for declaration that, the plaintiff is the owner of 16 annas property, as described in the schedule "Ka" to the plaint, and that the deed Nos. 5067, 5069 and 5071 registered in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Savar and the deed Nos. 3038 and 3039 regigtered in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Kalampur, Dhamrai, Dhaka, were forged, fabricated and by that deeds, the plaintiff's title in the suit property has not been affected in any manner. All these deeds were registered on 3-6-1981. Moreover, the plaintiff has described his case in his plaint as well as at paragraph No.2 of the revisional application. I have gone through the facts narrated in the plaint, which need not be repeated here for the sake of brevity. 

 6. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.135 of 2004, before the District Judge, Dhaka, which was heard by the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. In appeal, the plaintiff has given additional evidence by adducing his mother (defendant No. 7), who has deposed before the appellate court as PW On the other hand, the defendants have also given additional evidence before the appellate court, by producing one Poresh Chandra Mondal and Md Amir Uddin (DW 6 and 7), being the attesting witnesses of the questioned documents. After hearing the parties and having considered the evidence on record, the appellate court concurred with the findings of the trial court and has dismissed the appeal, thereby it has affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court, vide its judgment and decree dated 10-4-2014 (decree signed on 15-4-2014). 

 9. Learned Advocate Mr Sherder Abul Hossain appeared on behalf of the petitioner. He, having placed the revisional application and other materials on record, mainly submits that, admittedly Rakhal Chandra Mondal was the owner of 16 annas (the entire) suit property and he died leaving his wife Laxmi Bewa and the plaintiff Sree Tusta Chandra Mandal, as owners of the suit property. He next points out that, the plaintiff was minor, therefore, he had no knowledge about the 5 sale deeds described in the schedule "Kha" to the plaint. He proceeds on that, the defendants had created those forged documents. However, the plaintiff had to file Title Suit No.38 of 2000 seeking permanent injunction against the defendants and the defendants filed written statements in that suit, claiming title in the suit property alleging that, the suit property was sold to them, by the plaintiff's mother as his guardian, appointed in the Guardianship Case No.1316 of 1980 and that she had also obtained sale permission on 3-1-1984. The learned Advocate next submits that, the plaintiff has thus come to know about these 5 disputed sale deeds and had filed the instant suit seeking declaration of his title as owner of 16 annas of the suit property as well as for further declaration that the aforesaid 5 deeds were forged, fabricated and not binding upon him. The learned Advocate, having drawn my attention to the documents maintained in the LCR, continues that, in the Guardianship Case, name of Laxmi Bewa appears only as petitioner and there is no name of any respondents, vide Exhibit "Da". He next refers to the certified copy of the Suit Register of Permission Miscellaneous Case No. 1688 of 1980 and submits that, it does not prove that Laxmi Bewa had filed this case or that she got permission to sell the suit property. Therefore, the sale to the defendants was not valid and all these documents were obtained by resorting to fraud and forgery by the defendants. He also submits that, the defendants were not in possession of the suit property, while the DW 1, who was borgader, has proved the plaintiffs possession in the suit property. But, this has not been taken into consideration by the courts below. He next submits that, this is a case where the validity of the disputed sale deeds has been challenged on the ground of forgery, but not on the execution of these disputed documents by a validly appointed guardian in as much as the plaintiff does not admit appointment of his mother Laxmi Bawa as his guardian. Therefore, this case should fall under Article 120 Schedule- I of the Limitation Act, 1908, not under Article 44 Schedule- 1 of the said Act. He, therefore, submits that, both the courts below ought to have held that, the suit was not barred by limitation as per Article 44 of the Limitation Act, 1908. As such, he sums up that, the courts below have committed grave error of law and that has resulted in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He concludes that, this Rule has merit and the same may kindly be made absolute. 

 10. On the contrary, Mr MM Shafiullah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1(a) to 1(m) submits that, the plaintiff's mother, who was the defendant No. 7 before the court below, in this suit filed by the plaintiff (her son), but she herself did not file this suit questing the validity of the sale deeds described in schedule "Kha" to the plaint, nor had she appeared in the trial court to support the plaintiff's case. She has appeared as an witness for the plaintiff-appellant in Title Appeal No. 135 of 2004. He next refers to the deposition of Laxmi Bewa (mother of the plaintiff) wherein she has deposed (before the appellate court) that, “আমি আমার নাবালক পুত্রদ্বয়ের অভিভাবক হওয়ার জন্য জেলা জজ আদালতে ১৩১৬/৮০ নম্বর মামলা করেছিলাম । এই মামলায় আমি অভিভাবক নিযুক্ত হয়েছিলাম । আমার অভিভাবক নিযুক্ত আদেশ বিজ্ঞ জেলা জজ আদালত বাতিল করেন নাই।” Next referring to the said deposition the learned Advocate also points out that, during cross examination, this deponent has admitted before the appellate court that, “সাভারে দলিল করিয়া দিয়াছি। উহা বাদীকে বলি নাই । বাদী আমার পুত্র হয় ।”The learned Advocate further submits that, this admission of Laxmi Bewa, considered alongwith the deposition of defendant's witnesses and the documents proved by them, it is apparent that, the depositions of witnesses of the defendants have been corroborated by the plaintiff's mother. The fact that she had executed the aforesaid 5 sale deeds, as guardian of the minors and for the benefit of the minors, i.e for purchasing another house by the sale proceeds of the aforesaid kabala deeds, has also been proved, the learned Advocate also adds to his submission. Next, referring to the Suit Register of the Guardian-ship Case No. 1316 of 1980 (Exhibit "Da"), the learned Advocate for the opposite party submits that, the name of the petitioner alone will appear in the said case in as much as none else had contested for guardianship of the minors. There was no objection to her prayer for the guardianship, hence, there was no name in the column of respondent, in the suit register of the Guardianship Case). But, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has misinterpreted this document, before this Court, he further submits. The learned Advocate for the opposite party Nos. 1(a) to 1(m) also submits that, Laxmi Bewa, the mother of the plaintiff, was appointed as guardian of the minors plaintiff and the fact of the execution of the aforesaid 5 sale deeds were proved, as per provisions of section 68 of the Evidence Act, 1872, by producing the attesting witnesses, before the appellate court. Besides, he argues that, the plaintiff did not file this suit within 3 years after attaining majority i.e. before expiry of 1999, rather he has filed the suit on 7-2-2002, that is long after expiry of the period prescribed in Article 44, schedule 1 of the Limitation Act, 1908. The learned Advocate for the opposite party empathically submits that, since an appointment of guardianship has been proved by adequate evidence, therefore, the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the period of limitation shall be counted under Article 120, schedule 1 of the Limitation Act, 1908, is not correct. The learned Advocate also submits that, since the plaintiff's mother (defendant No. 7) had executed the questioned documents (Exhibit Gha series) therefore, she did not appear before the trial court to give deposition in favour of the plaintiff. This conduct of the executant Laxmi Bewa also proves that she had executed the aforesaid 5 sale deeds, while she has admitted that she has executed the 3 deeds in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Savar namely deed Nos. 5067, 5069 and 5071, although she had denied the execution of deed Nos. 3038 and 3039 in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Kalampur, Dhamrai, Dhaka. He proceeds on that, the defendants have proved execution of all the 5 deeds, by producing 2 attesting witnesses. 

 11. At this stage, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that, execution of 5 deeds in the office of 2 different Sub-Registrar's Office on the same date i.e. on 3-6-1981, proved that, the defendants have resorted to fraud and forgery in executing these deeds. Otherwise, he submits, why the executant should execute and register the deed Nos. 3038 and 3029 in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Kalampur, Dhamrai, Dhaka, although the property is situated within the jurisdiction of Savar Sub-Registrar office. In reply to this submission, the learned Advocate for the opposite party argues that, as per section 28 of the Registration Act, execution of these 2 deeds at Kalampur Sub-Registrar Office was permitted by law (at that line) and in support of his contention he has referred to 37 DLR (AD) 177: Syed Kawsar Ali vs Gahar Kazi and others. Besides, the learned Advocate for the opposite party submits that, the case of the defendant has duly been proved by submitting relevant DCR, mutation khatian, Khajna Dhakilas etc. and as well as the defendants have submitted all 5 original kabala deeds and all these were duly proved and were marked as exhibits by the trial court. He next refers to the examination of DW 4, Hazi Habibur Rahman, who has deposed in the trial court stating that, there was a dispute between the defendants and one Helal Uddin, who purchased some property of the deceased Rakhal Chandra Mondal from his second wife Sagor Bewa (Step-mother of the plaintiff) and a complaint case was filed before the Martial Law Court in the year 1982 and the dispute was referred to the Savar Union Parishad and the Union Parishad had resolved the dispute in an amicable settlement and the defendants got 1.83 decimals of land. As such, it will be evident from the evidence on record, in all the forums and in all cases, including the case filed for permanent injunction and before the Martial Law Court, the defendants have appeared and contested to protect their title in the suit property, since they are the bonafide purchaser for value. He next submits that, in cross examination of the deposition of Laxmi Bewa, she was asked as to whether she was willing to sent her thumb impression for expert opinion, but she did not sent the same, although she had agreed to sent, because if the same were sent for expert opinion, then it would have been revealed that she herself had executed all these disputed 5 sale deeds. He therefore, concludes that, this Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged. 

 13. I find that, the plaintiff's mother, who was the defendant No. 7, before the court below, has appeared as witness for the plaintiff-appellant in Title Appeal No. 135 of 2004, where she has admitted that, she had applied for appointment of guardianship of the minor plaintiff, vide Guardianship Case No. 1316 of 1980 and was appointed as guardian of the said minors. Her guardianship was not cancelled by the district court, she also admits. Although she had in the same breath deposed that, her guardianship was cancelled in a Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1981, but no such document was either filed by her, nor by the plaintiff-appellant. 

 15. Having considered the deposition of the defendant's witnesses, as recorded by the trial court as well as of two other DWs, who have deposed before the appellate court as the attesting witnesses, I find that the defendants have produced the 5 disputed sale deeds in original and proved all 5 title deeds before the trial court, marked as Exhibit "Gha" series. They have also placed and proved all these relevant documents connected to the sale. I also find that Poresh Chandra Mondal and Amir Uddin, who deposed as attesting witnesses before the appellate court, are attesting witnesses in all 5 documents and they have testified consistently about execution of these 5 deeds by Laxmi Bewa and the minor discrepancy that was found in the deposition of Amir Uddin (as regards the Registration Office) was not material, in as much as, due to elapse of a long time, the attesting witness Amir Uddin might have forgotten if these deeds were registered in one or two Sub-Registrar's Office. Moreso, when this is a matter of documentary evidence and this deponent could have given the name of both Sub-Registrars Offices by refreshing his memory. However, no material inconsistency has been found in their deposition. Besides, the documentary evidence as proved and marked as Exhibit-K to Z, clearly consistently and adequately proved the defendant's title and possession in the suit property, since the date of their purchase subject, however, to obtaining the sale permission. 

 In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 10-4-2014 (decree signed on 15-4-2014), passed by the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No.135 of 2004, dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 10-4-2004 (decree signed on 17-4-2004), passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Savar, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.36 of 2002, is hereby upheld.

lawyer:
M Qnamrul Hoque Siddique Advocate, instructed by Mvi, Md. Wahidullah Advocate-on-Record ......  For the Appellants. 
Md. Ali Reza Advocate, instructed by Ni. Bhuiyan Advocate-on-Record and Abdul Hye Bhuiyan Advocate-on-Record ......... For Respondent Nos. 1 (a) (i)- 1 (a) (vii) and 1 (b) - 1 (e) 
Respondent No. 2-4 ....... None represented
parties:
Nazimuddin Mondal and another ------ Appellants
-Vs-
Kushal Mondal being Dead his heirs: 1 (a) Son Md. Nasaruddin @ Nazor Ali deing dead his heirs:1 (a) (i) . Md. Kurman Ali and others --------  Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in short, are that Kushal Mondal, predecessor of the respondents herein as plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No. 275 of 1975 in the Court of the then Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Rajshahi for declaration of title to the suit land. The plaintiff stated, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to one Askar Mondal, who possessed the same and died leaving behind his brother's son Saber Mondal. Saber Mondal during his lifetime used to possess the suit land and after his death his heir, the original plaintiff Kushal Mondal as his son inherited the property. During S.A. operation, the land in dispute was correctly recorded in the name of the plaintiff and, accordingly, he paid rent to the Government and the Government after accepting him as tenant granted rent receipts in his favour. During R.S. operation, the suit land was erroneously recorded in the name of the defendants. Accordingly, the plaintiffs title to the suit property was doused. Hence, the plaintiff filed the suit. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the disputed property originally belonged to Askar Mondal. But during his lifetime, he surrendered the same in favour of ex-landlord, who settled the same to one Chhoto Babu Mondal, who died leaving behind defendant Nos.1 and 4 as daughters and one Saira Bewa as wife. Saira Bewa gifted her share in favour of her grandsons, defendant Nos.2 and 3 and one Rahim Uddin Mondal, Rahim Uddin Mondal died leaving behind defendant No.5 as father and defendant No4 as mother. Accordingly, defendant Nos.1-5 had been possessing the suit land after acquiring the same and paid rent to the Government. The R.S. record of the sit property has correctly been published in the names of defendant and possession in the suit land and as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 III. That the defendants' claim was that their names were recorded in S.A. khatian and in support of their claim they called for the record from the local settlement office and it was evidently proved that the volume stood in the names of defendant Nos. 1-4 but the High Court Division without looking into this aspect made the Rule absolute and as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. 

 6. Mr. Md. Ali Reza, learned Advocate appearing for respondent Nos.1(a)(i)- 1(a)(vii) and 1(b)-1(e) made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He also submitted that Askar Mondal died leaving Saber Mondal as brother's son who inherited the property left behind by Askar Mondal and subsequently Saber Mondal died leaving son Kushal Mondal and the High Court Division rightly found that Saber Mondal possessed the suit land for more than 12(twelve) years and the S.A. record was duly prepared in the name of the son of Suber Mondal and he paid rents to the Government and, accordingly, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. He further submitted that all the P.Ws. categorically proved that the plaintiff is owning and possessing the suit land and the S.A. khatian was rightly prepared in the name of the plaintiff and the defendants miserably failed to prove the basis of the recording of the R.S. khatian in respect of the suit land in their names and accordingly the High Court Division disbelieved the case of the defendants and rightly made the Rule absolute which calls for no interference by this Division. He submitted that the defendants have miserably failed to prove that the original owner of the suit land namely Askar Mondal surrendered the suit land in favour of the ex-landlord and the defendants failed to adduce any documentary evidence and also failed to examine any pertinent witness to prove this issue and as such, the High Court Division has rightly made the Rule absolute which calls for no interference by this Division. He submitted that the defendants have failed to prove by adducing any documentary evidence that after surrender of the suit land by Askar Mondal, when the ex-landlord took the same in his khas possession and also when he settled the same to Chhoto Babu Mondal (the predecessor-in-interest of defendant No.1-5), and the trial Court and the High Court Division rightly found that that the defendants miserably failed to prove their case and, therefore, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute which calls for no interference by this Division. He submitted that P.V1s.4 and 5 are independent witnesses who clearly stated in the deposition that the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land and they have land near the suit land and that the High Court Division rightly believed the evidentiary value of the deposition of these two independent witnesses and observed that the witnesses of the defendants contradicted themselves in their depositions in respect of possession of the suit land their testimony is not cogent and credible and, therefore the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute which calls for no interference by this Division. He also submitted that the Court of appeal below, as the final Court of fact, did not discuss and consider a single witness examined by the contesting parties while reversing the judgment of the trial Court as is required by Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He lastly submitted that the High Court Division as well as the trial Court rightly came to a finding that the plaintiff proved his title and possession in the suit land and the defendants have miserably failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land and hence the impugned judgment calls for no interference by this Division. 

 7. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record. 

 8. At the outset we are constrained to hold that the finding of the High Court Division to the effect that, "It is the established principle of civil law that the R.S. records of rights have got no presumptive value of its correctness "such observation is clearly contrary to section 114 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, of which the relevant provisions are reproduced here:- 

 144. Revision of record-of-rights -(1) The Government may in any case if it thinks fit make an order directing that a record-of-rights in respect of any district, part of a district or local area be prepared or revised by a Revenue-officer, in accordance with such rule as may be made by the Government in this behalf. 

 (4) When an order is made under sub-section (1), the Revenue-officer shall record in the record-of-rights to be pre-pared or revised in pursuance of such order such particulars as may be pre-scribed. 

 (5)When a record-of-rights has been prepared or revised so as to contain or include therein the particulars referred to in sub-section (4), and rents assessed or re-assessed under sub-section (4a), the Revenue-officer shall publish a draft of the record-of-rights so pre-pared or revised in the prescribed manner and for the prescribed period and shall receive and consider any objections which may be made to any entry therein or to any omissions therefrom during the period of such publication. 

 (7) When all such objections and appeals have been considered and dis-posed of according to such rules as the Government may make in this behalf, the Revenue-officer shall finally frame the record and shall cause such record to be finally published in the pre-scribed manner and the publication shall be conclusive evidence that the record has been duly prepared or revised under this section. 

 (8) When a record-of-rights has been finally published under sub-section(7), the Revenue-officer shall, within such time as the Director of Land Records and Surveys may fix in this behalf, make a certificate stating the fact of such final publication and the date thereof and shall date and subscribe the same with his name and official title. 144A. Presumption as to correctness of record of rights-Every entry in a record-of-rights prepared or revised under section 144 shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry, and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect." 

 11. Hence, there can be no doubt that the record of rights in the names of the defendants creates a rebuttable presumption in their favour. 

 12. The plaintiff claims title in the suit land by way of inheritance from Saber Mondal who was the nephew of the original owner, namely Askar Mondal. The S.A. record was in the name of the plaintiff, but the R.S. record for the suit land was wrongly in the name of the defendants. On the other hand the defendants claim that the original owner Askar Mondal surrendered the suit land in favour of the superior landlord who settled the land in favour of Chhoto Babu Mondal more than 50 years previously and the land is now in the possession of the successors of said Chhoto Babu Mondal. They also claimed that the documents produced by the plaintiff were forged. 

 14. The moot question in the instant case is whether the plaintiff was able to prove that title in the suit land passed to him through his father Saber Mondal who was the brother of the original owner Askar Mondal. The trial Court decreed the suit upon observing that, "It has not been challenged by the defendants that the plaintiff is not the brother's son of Askar Mondal." The trial Court also relied on the fact that the S.A. record was in the name of the plaintiff, which was also supported by rent receipts showing that the government realised rent for the suit land from the plaintiff up to 1967 (1374 B.S.) admitting the plaintiff as tenant. The trial Court also observed that the defendants, did not adduce any evidence to prove that the ex-landlord got the suit land in his khas possession after surrender by Askar Mondal or that Chhoto Babu Mondal got settlement. 

 17. Although the plaintiff claimed title to the land with support from Ext-1 the S.A. Khatian, he did not challenge the genuineness of the original volume of the S.A. record, which was, produced before the appellate Court at the instance of the defendants. The appellate Court found on penisal of the volume in question that the suit property was duly recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 1-4 in the name of one Saira Bewa, wife of Chhoto Babu Mondal. In allowing the appeal by the defendants, the appellate Court took into consideration the rent receipts produced by the defendants showing payment of rent to the government. 

 18. In view of the above facts and circumstances, it is abundantly clear that the judgment and decree of the trial court was patently erroneous and based upon misreading of evidence. The appellate Court properly reversed the judgment of the trial Court. Evidently the claim of the plaintiff was falsified by the production of the S.A. record of rights, which falsified the claim of the plaintiff and, on the other hand, proved that the S.A. records were in the names of the defendants.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3214 of 2013
parties:
Abdul Gafur Pramanik and another ------ Petitioners
-Vs-
The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Sirajgonj and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the plaintiffs claimed that the suit plot belonged to the CS recorded tenant, Bhubon Chandra Sarker who sold 20 decimals land out of 40 decimals by a kabala dated 05.05.1926 to his brother's son, Nikunja Sarker. The said original owner died leaving no issue and his remaining 20 decimals land devolved upon his brother's son, Nikunja. Thus, the entire plot was acquired by Nikunja by purchase and inheritance. One the death of Nijunja, the suit plot devolved upon his two minor sons, Badal and Buddeshwar. The SA record for the suit plot was wrongly prepared in the name of the Government, but subsequently the R.S. record was correctly prepared in the name of the said Badal and Budhiswar. By taking advantage of the wrong S.A. record, one Mozibur Rahman and his wife, Asia Khatun managed to get permanent lease from the Government by a registered lease deed dated 11.11.1992. For avoiding any unnecessary dispute, Buddeshwar got a kabala deed dated 04.05.1992 executed by the said lessee on payment of taka 5000. During his possession and title over the share, Buddeshwar by kabala dated 18.05.1994 sold the suit land to the plaintiffs. After purchase, the plaintiffs had been in possession. But, on 12.08.1994, defendant No.3, the Assistant Commissioner of Land issued a show cause notice upon the plaintiffs about initiating a criminal proceeding on the allegations that the plaintiffs fraudulently purchased the suit plot; hence the suit. 

 5. Mr. SK. Md. Sirajul Islam, appearing for the petitioners, submits that the High Court Division erred in not holding that though the SA Khatian was prepared in the name of the Government, but the RS Khatian No.478 was rightly prepared and published in respect of 40 decimals land in the names of the said two sons of Nikunja Sarker, i.e. Buddeshwar and Badal Chandra which proved that the SA Khatian was wrongly prepared in the name of the Government. He further submits that the High Court Division fell into error in not holding that taking advantage of the said wrong preparation SA Khatian, the Government gave pattan to one Mojibur Rahman on 11.11.1992 and the claim of the plaintiffs was that for getting rid of the said illegal pattan, the plaintiffs on 04.05.1994 purchased 20 decimals land in question from said Mojibur Rahman and thereafter, the plaintiffs purchased the said property from Buddeshwar on 18.05.1994 and instituted the original suit for declaration of title in accordance with law and that was supported by the evidence of PW1. The learned Advocate further submits that by adducing evidence PW2 proved the plaintiffs' possession over the suit land though the Government erroneously cancelled the lease deed in holding that the suit land had no legal value in the eye of law and the predecessor of the plaintiffs did not get title of the suit land. 

 10. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in his impugned judgment made the Rule absolute on holding that the Appellate Court failed to consider that the original tenant having died leaving no issue and as such, his tenancy was terminated and the suit land was correctly recorded in the name of the Government during SA operation who is in possession through its lessee. 

 11. In the above context, we have perused the record. The impugned judgment shows that that plaintiff failed to prove the fact that Nikunja was the brother's son of Bhubon Chandra Sarker and as such, the suit land measuring .20 acres was never inherited by Nikunja and the same has been possessed by the Government through local chairman who conceded that he (DW5) is possessing the same under the instruction of local revenue authority. The impugned judgment further shows that the suit land measuring 20 decimals out of 40 decimals has not been specified by demarcation and as such, a simple suit for declaration of title is not maintainable in its present form and the suit is hit by the provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act.
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

parties:
The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Works, Bangladesh Sachibalaya, Dhaka. ----- Appellant
-Vs-
Sabia Yasmin Hena and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
5. The Rule was opposed by the writ respondent government, contending inter alia that the property is an abandoned property within the meaning of P.O. No. 16 of 1972 as the original owner was not present in Bangladesh and never applied for release of her property after the promulgation of P.O. No. 16 of 1972. No application of the alleged son of the owner was ever received by the Government at any material point of time for release of the property. No agreement for sale was ever executed by the original owner with the writ petitioner and moreover the original owner was not present in Bangladesh to execute any deed of agreement with the writ petitioner. The alleged sale deed has been created by the writ petitioner which has not been executed by the original owner and moreover the alleged sale deed has been created in contravention of the provisions of law. The inclusion of the property in the gazette is lawful as the whereabouts of the original owner were not known and she lost control, management and supervision of the property in person and the owner was not a national of Bangladesh. The writ petitioner also accepted the demand note of the Government to pay rents and also rents to the Government as occupier of this abandoned property. Further, the Government asserted that on his own statement the writ petitioner admitted that the case property is an abandoned property because admittedly the original owner Mohsina Khatoon was not possessing the case land at the relevant time and from his own statement it is also apparent that according to him the title to the case holding is still lying with Mohsina Khatoon because the writ petitioner has not yet established his title on the basis of his so called bainapatra by getting a decree from a competent civil court. The case property by operation of law vested in the Government. That means the Government stepped into the shoes of the original owner of the case property and the writ petitioner, having no title to the same, cannot challenge the action of the Government. The writ petitioner is a third party and on his representation the property cannot be released. 

 8. Mr. Ekramul Haque, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the appellant-Government submits that the High Court Division erred in law in not taking into consideration the list prepared under Ordinance No. 54 of 1985, which carries a conclusive presumption that the property has been rightly enlisted as an abandoned properties; it also did not take into Consideration that the writ-petitioner (respondent herein) admitted that he occupied the said property illegally in 1972 and residing therein though subsequently he started paying rents as a lessee of the Government. Such admission of the writ petitioner justifies the presumption that the property has been rightly enlisted as an abandoned property. He also submits that the writ petitioner is an illegal occupier of the case property since 1972 and subsequently claiming the property by dint of a bainapatra, allegedly executed by the original owner Mohsina Khatoon and, as such, the High Court Division came to an erroneous conclusion that the property is an not abandoned property, without considering that mere bainapatra under no circumstances can be construed as a title document. He further submits that the original owner, Mrs. Mohsina Khatoon, having not co me forward to claim the property by filing an application under section 7 of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 before the Court of Settlement within time for exclusion of the said property from such list or to return the same to her on the ground that the same is not an abandoned property and that being an alternative efficacious remedy, invoking writ jurisdiction under article 102 of the Constitution is not at all maintainable. He next submits that the writ petitioner not being the owner cannot acquire fundamental right by purchase of an abandoned property in 1984. Finally he submits that the application filed before the Court of Settlement being rejected as being barred the High Court Division cannot act as an appellate Court to determine the facts of its own. The High court Division under article 102 of the Constitution can interfere with the decision of the court of Settlement only if the writ petitioner could make out a case that the Court of Settlement acted without jurisdiction and made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any material evidence causing prejudice to the complaining party or that the Court of settlement acted malafide and in violation of natural justice. Thus he submits that the appeal be allowed for ends of justice. 

 11. From the record it also appears that the writ petitioner admitted that the vigilant team of the Government visited the case property in 1975 to whom the writ petitioner produced the bainapatra and asserted that he had been living there in part performance of the con-tract but the vigilant team in the absence of proper title deed directed him to vacate the case property as he was possessing the same as an unauthorized occupant. Thus he was compelled to agree that he would stay there as a lessee of the government on payment of regular rents, and as such he started paying rents as a lessee of the said abandoned property. Subsequently the writ petitioner claimed that Mrs. Mohsina Khatoon executed a sale deed in his favour on 12.06.1981 and also executed a document for registration of the same before the Sadar Sub-Registrar, Dacca. Thus the writ petitioner claims that the prop-is not an abandoned property at all within the meaning of PO 16 as Mrs. Mohsina Khatoon was available in Bangladesh and she executed a sale deed in his favour and she is possessing the said property. 

 16. The writ petitioner did not annex any document with the writ petition before the High Court Division to prove that Mrs. Mohsina Khatoon, the admitted owner, was very much available in Bangladesh during the war of liberation and/or till PO 16 was enacted. He also failed to produce any document that the whereabouts of Mrs. Mohsina Khatoon was very much known. When the writ petitioner failed to establish/prove the where about of Mrs. Mohsina Khatun, the real owner of the abandoned property in question were known to everybody during the war of liberation and she is a citizen of Bangladesh and she is in possession of the property, there is no illegality to treat the same as an abandoned property under the PO 16. Moreover on the face of admission of the writ petitioner that he is a lessee under the Government and he took lease admitting the same as an abandoned property the writ petitioner has no right to ask for release of the property to him as the rightful owner of the same. Moreover, under no circumstances he can claim that he is the owner of the property on the basis of an unregistered Bainapatra, in the absence of any valid title deed acquiring title before PO 16 of 1972 came into force or enlisting the same as an abandoned property As such, he has no fundamental right for which he could invoke article 102 of the constitution claiming violation of fundamental right.

caseno:
First Appeal No. 25 of 2015.
Civil Rule No. 45(FA) 2015.
parties:
Khokon Chandra Bhawal and others-------Plaintiff-Appellants
Vs
Md Gias Uddin and others--------Defendant-Respondents
full_judgment:
Fatema Najib J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 24-11-2014 passed by learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 18 of 2011 dismissing the suit. 

 2. The appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 18 of 2011 against the respondents as defendants for declaration of title in respect of suit land and further declaration that the compromise decree passed by learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 is illegal, collusive, void, and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 4. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land of CS plot No. 1827 measuring 50 decimals along with other lands was originally belonged to Nizamuddin and accordingly CS Khatian No. 142 was recorded in his name. Nizamuddin transferred the suit land by registered Mortgage Deed being No. 5146 on 29-8-1925 to one Wahed Ali. An amicable partition was made among the brothers of Wahed Ali in respect of suit land along with other undisputed lands and through an amicable partition Durjon, brother of Wahed Ali got the suit land. Durjan died leaving behind two sons namely, Jinnat Ali and Habibullah who later on sold the suit land to one Alim Mia son of Jonab Ali by registered Kabala No. 1836 dated 18-1-1956 and delivered possession to him, accordingly RS khatian No. 322 was prepared in the name of Mid alias Alimuddin. Alim Mia transferred the entire suit land by registered hebanama being No. 2582 on 14-6-1987 in favour of his wife Rabeya Khatoon, three sons—Sirajul, Samsul Hoq, Md Ramjan Hossain and four daughters—Hasenur Begum, Fatema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon and Shaheena Begum. In this way Rabeya and Ramjan got 15 decimals and 10 decimals of the suit land respectively. In the same way Hasenur, Fatema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon got together 11.15 decimals and Shaheena Begum got 13.75 decimals of land in the suit land. Subsequently Rabeya, Ramjan, Hasenur, Fatema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon mutated their names by declaration Deed No. 1148 dated 25-5-1993 and paid rents to the Government. Halima Khatoon sold her portion i.e 3 decimals of the suit land to one Abdul Ali by registered kabala being No. 3908 on 7-9-1995. Mst Shaheena Begum extinguished her share from the suit land by selling her portion to plaintiff No. 1, 2 and 3 through three registered Kabala Nos. 2669, 2670, 2671 all dated 18-7-1999 in equal share. Abdul Ali, who purchased the suit land from Halima sold his entire portion to plaintiff Nos. 1-3 by registered kabala No. 1031 on 1-4-2001. In this way the plaintiff No. 1-2 got 6 decimal each and plaintiff No. 3 got 51/4 decimals of land. Fatema Khatoon daughter of Alimuddin sold her entire share of suit land to Mafizul Islam, plaintiff No. 4 by saf-kabala on 12-9-1999. Ramjan (defendant No. 15) who got from his father Alimuddin by way of heba sold 3 decimals to plaintiff No.5 on 26-5-1999. Most. Rabeya, who got 15 decimals of land from her husband sold to the plaintiff Nos. 6-9 through three Kabalas on 23-6-1999. Hasenur Begum, who also got by heba sold it to one Habibullah and thereafter Habibullah sold it to the plaintiff No. 10 through Kabala No. 6568 on 9-12-2007. Ramjan (defendant No.15) and Halima Khatoon sold their remaining portion of land to the plaintiff No.11. Thus the plaintiffs have been possessing the entire suit land by mutating, paying rents, planting crops and taking loan from bank by mortgaging the suit land. The defendants were trying to demolish the boundary, then the plaintiffs filed the petition case No. 639 dated 1-12-2010. Thereafter the defendants were trying to disposes the plaintiffs and on 1-8-2010 the defendants disclosed that they got title over the suit land on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009, wherein the defendant Nos. 1-12 of the present suit as plaintiffs filed said Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 impleading the present defendant Nos. 4-7 and 13-15 as defendants. 

 5. The defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-11 con-tested the suit by filing a joint written statement. They denied material averments made in the plaint. The case of the defendants are that the suit land was originally belonged to Nizamuddin who died leaving behind two sons namely, Jonab Ali and Kamfu Mia. Janab Ali died leaving behind four sons namely, Alim Ali, Ayet Ali, Ameer Ali and Jamir All and two daughters namely, Topi Bibi, Aleshi Bibi. SA Khatian 321 was prepared in the name of Kamfu Mia and the aforesaid heirs of Jonab Ali. While in possession of 50% share i.e 25 decimals of suit land, Kamfu Mia died leaving behind wife Aimon Bibi and only son Hossain Mia. After death of Aimon bibi, Hossain ali got the share of Kamfu Mia and possessed the southern 25 decimals of the suit land. Hossain Ali died leaving behind six sons defendant Nos. 1-6 and one daughter defendant No. 11. Elachi bibi, daughter of Jonab Ali died leaving behind 4 brothers-Ameer Ali, Alim Ali, Ayet Ali, Jamir Ali and one sister Tohi Bibi. Ameer Ali died leaving behind 2 sons namely, Anwar Hossain, Amjad Hossain and one daughter Sahnaj i.e defendant Nos: 8-10. Thus defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-10 along with defendant No. 11 have been possessing 31decimals of land together with another piece of land by planting crops. The defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-10 executed power of attorney infavour of defendant No. 11 and 12 on 8-10-09 to look after the land and to deal with the suits. The defendants 1-6, 8-10 and 11 went to Tohsil Office to mutate their names and knew about wrong recording of RS Khatian in plaintiffs names. Thereafter the aforesaid defendants filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 420 of 2010 in which their names has been mutated and accordingly they paid tax, rent etc. The further case of the defendants is that Nizamuddin took loan 200 from one Wahed Ali subject to payment of 2% interest per month and accordingly a registered deed was executed between them on 29-8-1925. Subsequently, Nizamuddin paid the entire loan money to Wahid Ali and SA record was correctly prepared in the name of the heirs of Nizamuddin. Thus all the successive transfers were made on the basis of the said deed dated 29-8-1925 are illegal, inoperative and not binding upon the defendants. 

 9. Ms Nahid Yesmin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs-appellants primarily submits that the court below erroneously held that Deed No. 5146 dated 28-8-1925 (Exhibit-8(4) executed by Nizamuddin is not a mortgage deed but “জোত জমি বিক্রয় সুদি রেহানী” which effects or purports to effect the sale and said transaction cannot be treated as Mortgage as per section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act. She further submits that the learned Joint District Judge below failed to consider the oral and documentary evidence by which the plaintiffs were successfully proved their title and possession over the suit land. She finally argued further that the learned court below has committed gross illegality in not considering the stipulation made in the Deed in question that Nizamuddin sold the suit land, not mortgage the same to Wahid Ali. 

 11. Mr Md Delowar Hossain, the learned senior Advocate appearing for defendants respondents submits that the deed in question is a mortgage deed which purports to create a simple mortgage as the conditions mentioned in section 58(b) of the Transfer of Property Act. He submits further that no stipulation has been contained in the aforesaid deed that the mortgagor Nizamuddin delivered possession of the suit property to mortgagee, Wahid Ali. It was further stipulated that mortgagor took loan Taka 200 from the mortgagee subject to payment of 2% interest per month and the same loan will be returned to the mortgagee within Chaitra 1332 BS. It was also stipulated that in case of failure to pay the loan money, the mortgagee shall have right to get the property with intervention of the court. He next submits that the plaintiffs have miserably failed to produce any oral and documentary evidence to prove their title and possession of the suit land. He also submits that since the plaintiffs failed to prove by oral or documentary that the mortgagor Nizamuddin failed to pay loan with interest and the mortgagee got the suit land in auction through court, rather it was evident that SA Khatian was prepared in the name of legal heirs of Nizamuddin which clearly proved the title and possession of Nizamuddin predecessors of the defendants in the suit land. He further submits that the schedule of the present suit and the schedule of the earlier Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 are same and all the defendants were made parties either as plaintiffs or defendants in both the suits. The suit land on which the plaintiff claimed their title but their predecessors Wahed Ali did not acquire any title and possession. He finally submits that the court below has not committed error of law and facts and rightly found that the deed in question neither a Sale Deed nor a Deed of Mortgage by conditional sale. 

 13. From plain reading of the pleadings, documents produced and oral evidence adduced before court, it is admitted that the suit land measuring 50 decimals of land was originally belonged to Nizamuddin predecessors of the defendants, who executed a registered mortgage deed dated 29-8-1925 in favour of one Wahed Ali, Predecessors of the plaintiffs in respect of suit land by taking Taka 200 as loan subject to payment of interest @ 2% pin till realization of money. There was a clear stipulation for payment of interest on repayment of loan amount and in case of failure to repayment within specified time, 30th Chaitra, the mortgagee shall have a right to cause the mortgaged property to be sold with intervention of the court. 

 16. The core issue in this appeal is that whether the Deed No. 5146 dated 29-8-1925 (Exhibit-8/4) the basic document upon which the plaintiffs based their title is a Simple Mortgage or Mortgage by conditional sale. 

 20. There are 6 kinds of mortgage. Those are, Simple Mortgage, Mortgage by conditional sale, Usufructuary mortgage, English mortgage, Mortgage by deposit of title deeds and Anomalous mortgage. 

 26. The plaintiffs claimed that by successive transfers they became owner of the suit land. Since we have already observed that the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Wahed Ali did not become owner of the suit land in the first place, the subsequent transfers based on the transfers by dint of deed dated 19-8-1925 needs no discussion. It is hereby mentioned that the learned Advocate argued that Alim Mia grandson of Nizamuddin purchased the entire portion of suit land from Jinnat Ali, Habibulla, son of Durjon Ali, brother of Wahed Ali. Learned Advocate for the appellants tried to submit that since Wahed Ali became the owner of the suit land and his brother Durjon who also got it by amicable partition and then his heirs sold it to Alim Mia, son of Jonab Ali. But upon examining the photocopy of the deed No. 836 dated 18-1-1956 (Exhibit-9), it looks like a mortgage deed, not a sale deed. Md Osman Gani copyist, Sadar record room, District Registered office, Narayangonj as PW 5 deposed before court. He carried the volume wherein the description of the said deed was mentioned. He compared the description of the certified copy of the said deed with the volume and found similar. But the deed filed is not certified copy, it is a photocopy of the original. In his cross-examinations he has stated that he has no knowledge about the transaction and also did not know who are transferor and transferee. The said deed was not proved in accordance of law. So, we did not find merit in the argument made by the learned Advocate of the plaintiffs. 

 27. In the present suit the plaintiffs filed SA khatian (Exhibit-1/1) to prove their possession in the suit land. It appears that the said khatian was prepared in the name of Kamfu, and the heirs of Jonab Ali, who are sons of Nizamuddin which clearly proved the possession of the predecessor of the defendants and not the plaintiffs. It further proved that the original owner Nizamuddin never lost his title by executing the mortgage deed in favour of Wahed Ali. 

 28. Apart from the Exhibit-1/1, the plaintiffs to prove their possession examined one Md Abbas Ali, uncle of the plaintiff No. 2 as PW 2, who in his cross examination could not say the boundary of the suit land. Mr Sirazul Islam PW 3 and Md Delwar Hossain PW 4 in their cross-examination could not say the number of the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs quantam of land purchased by them. So, from the scrutiny the oral evidences it proved that no witnesses could say the quantum of the lands purchased by each plaintiffs and also the boundary of lands which do not prove the possession of the plaintiffs over the suit land. We have perused the Mutation Khatian, DCR, dhakilas land development tax (Exhibit-4 series) has been filed by the plaintiffs. Dhakhila, DCR, land development tax has been filed on the basis of Mutation Khatian Nos. 4632 (Exhibit-415), 16139 (Exhibit-4/7), 4690 (Exhibit-4/11). Those mutation Khatian were prepared on the basis of RS Khatian No. 322 (Exhibit-1/2). But the defendants have filed a Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 challenging that RS Khatian No. 322 was wrong. The said suit was decreed by the judgment and decree dated 1-8-2010 (Exhibit-5). On the basis of the said decree a Miscellaneous Case No. 420 of 10 Exhibit-uma(1) was initiated. In that Miscellaneous Case, Revenue Officer cancelled the Mutation Khatian prepared in the name of the plaintiffs and directed to mutate the names of the defendants in place of the plaintiffs. Against this order no step has been taken, by the plaintiff. Thus the defendants were successfully proved their possession in the suit land by filing Exhibit-uma(1). 

 29. The plaintiffs-appellants also prayed for declaration that the judgment and decree dated 1-8-2010 passed by learned Joint District Judge First Court in Title Suit No. 33J of 2009 is illegal collusive, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Perused the said judgment (Exhibit-5). It appears that the suit lands of previous suit and the suit land of the present suit are similar. All the defendants were made parties to previous suit either as plaintiffs or defendants. But the present plaintiffs were not made parties of in the previous suit. 

 30. We have already held that Wahed All did not acquire any title on the basis of the alleged mortgage deed and, as such, his legal heirs has no transferable interest to execute the deeds in favour of different people on different dates in respect of the suit land. We have also found that the plaintiffs have failed to prove the deeds in accordance of law and their possession in the suit land on the basis thereof. Thus the learned Sub-ordinate Judge did not commit any error or illegality in dismissing the suit. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge, of course, did not consider the prayer made by the plaintiffs as regards declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 is collusive, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Since we have found that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their title and possession over the suit land as such the plaintiffs have no locus-standi to challenge the decree obtained by the defendants in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009. 

 32. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree dated 24-11-2014 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 18 of 2011 is affirmed. The connected rule being Civil Rule No. 45(F) 2015 is discharged and the order of status-quo granted at the time of admission of the appeal is hereby vacated.

Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties No.1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 20.04.2015 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Rajbari, in Miscellaneous Appeal No.05 of 2010 dismissing the appeal affirming the judgment and order dated 01.02.2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1St Court, Rajbari in Miscellaneous Case NO.06 of 2006 arising out of Title Suit No.05 of 1997 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties No.1-3 as plaintiffs instituted the original Partition Suit being No.05 of 1997 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Rajbari against the defendant-petitioners and others. In that suit the plaintiffs for want of getting a separate shaham in respect of the land described in the schedule of the plaint submitted their pleadings and ultimately that suit was decreed by the learned trial Judge on 20.05.1999 and decree was signed on 08.07.1999. After getting the decree the plaintiffs being not satisfied filed a Title Appeal being No.52 of 1999 in the Court of learned District Judge, Rajbari and the learned appellate court allowed the appeal ex-parte and modified the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. Thereafter, the present petitioners filed a Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the 1StCourt of learned Joint District Judge, Rajbari for setting aside the judgment and decree being Miscellaneous Case No.06 of 2006. The learned trial Court after examining the witnesses disallowed the miscellaneous case by his judgment and order dated 01.02.2010. 

 6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original case filed under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and subsequent appeal committed illegality and irregularity resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the petitioners were admittedly defendants to the original partition suit, but there is no service of 

 7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel on behalf of the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that neither the trial court nor the lower appellate court during disposal of the original case and its subsequent appeal committed any illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the summons were duly served upon the defendant-petitioners in their own address under Order V rule 17 and 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure and both the courts below being satisfied opined that, in despite of service of notice upon the defendants; suppressing the facts they have filed the original miscellaneous case and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate in support of this submissions referred a decision of our Apex Court reported in 4 MLR (AD) 405. 

 9. Having gone through the papers on records it transpires that the present petitioners who were the defendants to the original Partition Suit being No.05 of 1997 raised a specific plea that, in that suit there was no service of summons notice upon them and for the reason stated, they were in the dark about the original suit and its decree. It was further case of the defendant-petitioners that in the subsequent appeal which was decreed in modified form was also not within the knowledge of them inasmuch as there was no service of summons notice upon them and in collusion with the process-server of the court the summons notices were suppressed by the plaintiffs. 

 10. On meticulous consideration over the relevant papers it appears that after the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No.52 of 1999 the original case record was sent back to the trial court. It is obvious to note that the decree was passed in the preliminary form and before its final decree the defendant-petitioners instituted the original Miscellaneous Case No.06 of 2006 under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the service of notice upon them. It is further noticed that the learned trial court bypassing the mandatory provisions of law as incorporated in Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure only on point of limitation disallowed the case. Subsequently; while the matter was placed before the lower appellate court in the form of appeal, the learned appellate court below in slip shod manner without proper appreciation of law as provided in the relevant provisions laid down in Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure decided the merit of the appeal against the appellants therein. 

 11. It is a fact that, in the original suit the service of summons was allegedly done under Order V rule 17 and 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure and subsequent to that, the defendants challenging that service of notice; instituted the Miscellaneous Case being No.06 of 2006 before the learned trial court and in that case it was their pleading that in fact there was no service upon them and the serving officer in collusion with the plaintiff served the summons notice after hanging. In the instant nature of case limitation is no doubt immaterial if it is proved that in fact there is no service of summons upon the defendants. The burden of proof in the instant case lies upon the plaintiffs to prove that in fact the service was done and the defendants suppressing the facts of , service of notice upon then raised their plea on non-service of summons. It was 

 15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 20.04.2015 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Rajbari, in Miscellaneous Appeal No.05 of 2010 dismissing the appeal affirming the judgment and order dated 01.02.2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, IS` Court, Rajbari in Miscellaneous Case No.06 of 2006 arising out of the Title Suit No.05 of 1997 is hereby set aside.

parties:
Md. Yousuf Ali Khan ------ Plaintiff-Petitioner
VERSUS
Bibi Quamrunnesa and others ------ Defendant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman, J: The instant Rule has been obtained at the instant of the plaintiff-petitioner challenging the legality and propriety of the Judgment and decree dated 18.09.2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.03 of 2012 against the compromise decree made under order 23 Rule 3 read with section 89A of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. The material facts, relevant for disposal of the instant Rule, as have been derived from the revisional application, succinctly are, that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted the Title Suit No.266 of 2005 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka against the defendant Bibi Quamrunnesa herein opposite party No.1 and others for Specific Performance of Contract. The said suit was transferred and renumbered as Title Suit No.187 of 2011. Eventually, the said suit again was transferred and re-numbered as Title Suit No.03 of 2012 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka, after setting aside the Judgment and decree dated 28.09.2011 and 04.10.2011 respectively. 

 3. The plaint case in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to the defendant-opposite party No.1 Bibi Quamrunnessa who had got permanent lease of the Suit Property vide registered Deed No.6675 dated 27.04.1966 from the erstwhile Dhaka Improvement Trust (now RAJUK). Thereafter she builds one storied building on the land. She executed a Bainapatra on 16.01.1995 with the plaintiff fixing total consideration money of Tk. 35,00,000/- out of which she received Tk. 20,00,000/- with stipulation that she will pay the whole dues loan money of the House Building Finance Corporation. She would also take sales permission from the RAJUK. The defendant had also received further consideration money time to time from the plaintiff-petitioner. The defendant thereafter started dilly-dally tactics to register the deed. However, she at a point of time demanded more extra money out of consideration of the agreement. 

 11. The present opposite party No.6 as 3rd party on 03.05.2012 filed a Miscellaneous Case being No.16 of 2012 under Order 9 Rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the Court of Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka for setting aside the Judgment and Decree dated 28.09.2011 passed in Title Suit No.187 of 2011 however, the said Miscellaneous Case again re-numbered as Miscellaneous Case No.11 of 2012. 

 12. The Opposite Party No.6 on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner fraudulently filed a written objection in the said Miscellaneous Case. Eventually, on 18.09.2012 the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka set aside the Judgment and decree dated 28.09.2011 passed by him in Title Suit No.187 of 2011. Thereby restored the Title Suit No.187 of 2011 in its original file and number. 

 13. Thereafter, the 3rd party filed an application in Title Suit No.187 of 2012 for addition of party which was allowed by the Court adding the petitioner 3rd party as defendant No.6 in the suit. After restoration the suit the same was renumbered as Title Suit No. 03 of 2012 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka. 

 15. The learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka on 18.09.2012 took upon the case for hearing and directed the office to transfer the record of decree Jari case No.10 of 2011 to his Court for hearing and order. Accordingly title suit No.3 of 2012 along with execution case No.10 of 2011 were placed before the Court for hearing and Order. 

 16. Thereafter, the plaintiff Yousuf Ali was examined by the Court as PW-1 in support of compromise petition and Mr. Abdul Momen was examined on behalf of the defendant No.6. The learned Judge after considering the testimony of P.W. and D.W. and considering the materials on record by its Judgment and decree dated 18.09.2012 dismissed the Title Suit No. 03 of 2012 arising out of Title Suit No. 187 of 2011 on the basis of compromise petition and thereby accepted the compromise application and declared that the sale deed being No.11216 and sale deed No. 1099 dated 01.12.2011 executed and registered on 29.11.2011 before the Sub-Registry Office, Gulshan, Dhaka through execution case No. 10 of 2011 arising out of 187 of 2011 is void and cancelled and directed the said Sub-Registrar to record the same in the Balaam Books within 7(seven) days and inform the Court accordingly. 

 17. The present petitioner being aggrieved by the Judgment and decree dated 18.09.2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court and Arbitration Court, Dhaka passed in Title Suit No.03 of 2012 and decree drawn upon in Title Suit No.03 of 2012 on the basis of the solenama under order 23 Rule 3 read with section 89A of the Code of Civil Procedure preferred the instant revisional application before this Court and obtained the instant Rule. 

 19. He has further submitted that the opposite party No.6 was not a party in the suit for Specific Performance of Contract however, he filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure having without any locus-standi but the Court below beyond the procedure of law and behind the plaintiff petitioner allowed the application at the instance of 3rd party and set aside the judgment and decree dated 28.09.201 1 and 04.10.2011 respectively, hence, the Court below has committed serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice in setting aside the same passed by the Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.187 of 2011. The defendant No.6 most illegally having no locus-standi not only setting aside the Judgment and decree dated 28.09.2011 passed in favour of the plaintiff petitioner rather, he has proceeded further to set aside the consequence of the original decree which has been passed in favour of the plaintiff in Title Suit No.187 of 2011. 

 20. He has further added that the defendant No. 6 has compelled the plaintiff petitioner on fear of life to put his signature in the compromise petitioner as high ups of the Army. He has also pointed that decree drown up on 18.09.2012 in Title Suit No.03 of 2012 being  3rd party and obtained Judgment and decree to the effects that the title suit No. 187 of 2011 is dismissed in terms of compromise and thereby declared the registered' deed No.1099 dated 01.12.2011 registered in the office of Sub-Registrar, Gulshan, Dhaka which can not be passed in accordance with law as the instance of the 3rd party defendant No. 6 who is neither vendor nor purchaser of the suit property, not only that he has no locus-standi to be a defendant as third party to set aside the Judgment and decree and obtained the compromise because during the compromise decree he got no title over the suit property and, as such, the Judgment and decree dated 18.09.2012 is liable to be set aside. 

 25. We have gone through the Judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 03 of 2012 under Order 23 Rule 3 read with section 89A of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 28. Considering the provision of the section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure as quoted here in above we find that the impugned Judgment and decree passed by the Joint District Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 03 of 2012 setting aside the Judgment and decree passed in title suit No. 187 of 2011 upon a compromise application which is not revisable. 

 30. More-so, the petitioner herein made some allegations against the 31-d party defendant No. 6 in the paragraph No. 9, 10 and 11 of the revisional application. It has categorically mentioned in the revisional application that the defendant No. 6 who was added party in the suit No.187 of 2011 he was neither plaintiff nor defendant in the suit. Besides, it has submitted that he has no personal interest and title nor his department has any right, title and interest over the suit property. 

 Furthermore, we are of the opinion that on perusal of the allegation as made in the revisional application it is crystal clear that said allegations was not tested in Court of Original Jurisdiction therefore, it should not be decided without appreciating the evidence in Revisional Jurisdiction.
