parties:
MUNTASIR MAMUN 
V. 
JUDGE, ARTHA RIN ADALAT NO.3, DHAKA AND OTHERS
full_judgment:
2. Short facts, relevant for the disposal of the Rule, are that, the National Credit and Commercial Bank Limited, through its Motijheel Branch, Dhaka (respondent nos. 2 and 3), filed Artha Rin Suit No. 584 of 2013 before the 3rd Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka against two defendants for realization of loan amount Tk. 4,33,73,200.25 as on 31.03.2013. In the said Suit, the petitioner was impleaded as defendant no.2 on the ground that the he had executed personal guarantee and deposited title deeds in respect of his property for securing the said loan obtained by defendant No. 1. In the said suit, the petitioner filed written statement denying the material averments in the plaint as well as stating that he did not execute any personal guarantee and that he did not mortgage any property by depositing title deed to secure the said loan of defendant no. 1. It was further stated that, the letter of guarantee as produced before the Adalat by the plaintiff bank was a forged document. In the course of hearing of the suit, the petitioner, on 06.07.2014, filed two applications for seeking a direction from the Adalat upon the Bank to furnish the copy of the original letter of guarantee as allegedly executed by the petitioner and to send the same to the hand-writing expert for examining the genuineness of the signature of the petitioner on the same contending, inter alia, that the petitioner's signatures on other documents, e.g. loan application etc., lying with the another branch of the bank, namely Jubilee Road Branch, Chittagong, do not tally with the signatures on the said letter of guarantee. Upon such applications, the Adalat, after hearing the parties, rejected the same vide impugned order dated 31.03.2015 mainly on the ground that the petitioner was filing such applications for delaying the suit. Being aggrieved by the impugned order, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the aforesaid Rule. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this Court, vide ad-interim order dated 17.06.2015, stayed further proceedings of the said suit for a period of 03 (three) months, which was subsequently extended time to time. 

 The Rule is opposed by Mr. Mohammad Akbar Hossain, learned advocate appearing for the plaintiff bank, by filing affidavit-in-opposition mainly contending that since the petitioner deposited title deeds of certain property with the bank to secure the loan obtained by the defendant no.1, the petitioner has no case before this Court. 

 3. Mr. Lokman Karim, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner, drawing this Court's attention to the impugned order as well as averments of the petitioner in the written statement, submits that, specific case of the petitioner as defendant no.2 before the Adalat is that the petitioner never secured the loan obtained by defendant No. 1 in the said case by any means. According to him, the further averment of defendant no.2 in the said case is that, this petitioner never executed any personal guarantee or deposited any title deed to secure the said loan. Learned advocate submits that, though the petitioner deposited title deed in respect of a loan obtained by the petitioner from Jubilee Road Branch, Chittagong, of the said bank, the said title deeds are now being used by the bank for the purpose of the loan obtained by defendant No.1 from its Motijheel Branch by fraudulently creating a letter of guarantee in the name of the petitioner. Therefore, according to him, the prayer of the petitioner before the Adalat was a very innocent prayer inasmuch as that the petitioner only wanted to ascertain the genuineness of the letter of guarantee as alleged to have been signed by the petitioner. 

 4. It appears from materials on record, in particular paragraph-14 of the written statement filed by this petitioner as defendant no.2 before the Adalat that, the specific case of the petitioner is that he never furnished any personal guarantee or never deposited any title deed to secure the loan obtained by defendant no.1 from the plaintiff bank's Motijheel Branch. Therefore, it appears that, the petitioner did have a case before the Adalat when he filed application for ascertaining the genuineness of the letter of guarantee alleged to have been signed by him to secure the said loan. In view of above, we do not find any reason as to why the Adalat rejected such application of the petitioner to have the genuineness of the alleged signature of the petitioner on the said letter of guarantee examined by the expert. This Court is of the view that, unless and until the genuineness of the said alleged signature of the petitioner on the said letter of guarantee is examined by expert, Adalat will not be in a position to determine whether in fact this petitioner did execute any personal guarantee to secure the said loan. In view of above, we find merit in the Rule and as such the same should be made absolute. 

 5. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. Thus, the impugned order 31.03.2013 as passed the Adalat is set aside. Accordingly, the said applications dated 06.07.2014 filed by the petitioner are hereby allowed. The Adalat concerned is directed to pass necessary orders directing the bank to produce the deposited title deeds of the petitioner as well as original copy of the letter of guarantee before it so that the genuineness of the petitioner's signature on the same is tested and examined by an expert and then proceed with the suit in accordance with law.

parties:
Abul Barik
Vs.
Abdul Jabbar and Others
full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party No.1 (now dead) one Abdul Jabbar as plaintiff instituted the Other Class Suit No. 225 of 2000 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Kishoreganj Sadar against the present petitioner for a declaration that the deed of exchange being No.6203 dated 19.09.2000 in the office of the Sub-registrar, Kishoreganj relating to the suit property is collusive and ineffective with a further prayer for recovery of khash possession in the suit property described in the schedule of the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to the father of the plaintiff namely Mali Hossain. At the demise of Mali Hossain his one wife, 08(eight) sons and 03 (three) daughters became the heirs. Among the heirs of the original owner by way of an amicable partition the brother of the plaintiff Bonde Ali obtained 333/4 decimals of land out of 45 decimals of land and the other sisters jointly obtained 111/4 decimals of land and possess their portion. Subsequently, by a sub-kabala deed dated 15.05.1980 Bonde All transferred 83/4 decimals of land to the northern side of two plots and handed over possession therein in favour of the purchaser-plaintiff. The plaintiff in respect of the property of his sisters borga possess 111/4 decimals of land. Among the sisters of the plaintiff, Amena Khatun and Rahima Khatun transferred their share in favour of their sister Jobeda Khatun and Jobeda Khatun subsequently by a sub-kabala dated 01.10.2000 transferred her land measuring 10 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff. The further case of the plaintiff is such that the plaintiff by way of sub-kabala dated 30.11.1998 purchased 25 decimals of land in the suit plot and possessed therein and in this way the plaintiff acquired 45 decimals of land in two plots. On 08.10.2000 the plaintiff was dispossessed by the defendant and the defendant without the knowledge of the plaintiff at night erected a tin-shed but in the suit property, having no manner of valid right, title, interest therein which constrained the plaintiff to institute the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendant-petitioner in short is thus that Bonde Ali is the full brother of the plaintiff who is the vendor of the defendant-petitioner. The suit land was acquired by Bonde Ali in his share amicably after the death of his father and thereafter on 19.09.2000 by way of a registered ewaj deed the defendant-petitioner acquired title and possession in the suit property. The defendant-petitioner obtained possession within the knowledge of the plaintiff and other villagers of the locality and through survey by a government-surveyor but the plaintiff out of ill-motive to grab the property suppressing the facts have instituted the suit. 

 4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after framing five different issues decided all the issues in favour of the plaintiff and decreed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 25.11.2004. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that both the courts below during passing the judgment and decrees in favour of the plaintiff committed illegality. The learned Advocate further submits that it is the settled principle of law that the plaintiff is to prove his own case and he is not entitled to get a decree on the weakness of the defendant. But the learned trial court shifted the responsibility of proving the case on the defendant illegally and subsequently the appellate court also disallowed the appeal without proper appreciation of law and thereby both the courts below committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiff examined 04(four) witnesses including himself as P.W.1 but he could not prove his plaint case and on the contrary the defendant examined two witnesses including the defendant No.1 as D.W.1 who successfully proved the case of the defendant. But the courts below on non-consideration and non-reading of evidence illegally decreed the suit. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the appellate court below in fact not at all discussed any evidence. The learned Advocate argued that, P.W.1 in his testimony did not state the time of his alleged dispossession but the learned trial court held that at night the dispossession took place. The 2nd witness of the plaintiff P.W.2 in his deposition did not state the day and date of dispossession and P.W.3 also did not state the specific day and date of dispossession. The last witness P.W.4 is the witness of a deed given by his mother dated 01.10.2000 and thus the courts below without proper assessment of evidence on records arrived an erroneous findings that the plaintiff have been successfully proved his possession and dispossession over the suit property. Furthermore; no boundary man as stated from the side of the plaintiff has deposed to prove the possession and dispossession of the plaintiff while the brother of the plaintiff-D.W.2 who was the vendor of the defendant-petitioner categorically proved the case of the defendant and disproved the case of the plaintiff. But the learned court below misdirected himself on such evidence and without any basis held that the defendant did not examine any witness to substantiate his case. The learned Advocate Mr. Moinuddin at a stage of his submissions submits that the most important witness of this case is D.W.2 who is the vendor of the defendant and this witness in his deposition specifically asserted that at the time of giving possession of the suit land to the defendant No.1 the plaintiff and his other brothers and sisters were present and there is no specific denial from the side of the plaintiff with regard to this which amounts to admission of the matter. In the plaint the plaintiff sought for three separate reliefs but the learned courts below without giving two reliefs gave only one relief which is vague and indefinite and that there was no separate issue even on the ewqjnatna deed of the defendant-petitioner and also there is no issue on possession and dispossession specifically. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument advanced from the side of the petitioner and submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality, irregularity or infirmity. The learned Advocate further submits that in disposing the appeal the learned lower appellate court in deciding the merit of the appeal committed no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned trial court during deciding the onus of proof committed no illegality, since it is the specific case of the defendant-appellant-petitioner that his predecessor-in-interest i.e. from whom he obtained the suit land acquired right, title, interest and possession in the disputed property by way of amicable partition between the co-sharers of the heirs of admitted original owner Male Hossain and it was further specific case of the present petitioner that by way of a registered that ewajnama deed dated 19.09.2000 the defendant-petitioner acquired right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and immediate after that ewajnama; the possession was delivered in favour of him and in exchange of a property the brother of the plaintiff-opposite party, Bonde Ali executed and registered the alleged ewajnama in his favour in respect of his property which he acquired. The learned Advocate submits that among the prayers of the plaintiff in the original suit although the trial court in respect of 'recovery of khash possession' passed his verdict in the order-portion of his judgment and decree but within the body of the judgment the learned trial court decided all; after proper evaluation of the evidence on record and that the plaintiff have valid right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and the defendant dispossessed the plaintiff at night and it is a bonafide omission of the learned trial court in the order-portion, despite; in the findings and decisions he has categorically arrived at a decision as to the matter of controversy between the parties and with regard to possession and dispossession of the suit property and although the learned court below not framed specific issue but he has categorically arrived at a decision as to the possession and dispossession in the suit property. The learned Advocate argued that the plaintiff to the suit during trial after adducing sufficient credible evidence in support of his case have successfully discharged his onus in proving his respective case and both the courts below on preponderance of evidence rightly decided the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal in favour of the plaintiff. Under the purview of Order V rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure the learned trial court rightly discussed and decided each and separate issue on the basis of the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties and no objection or challenge was raised from the side of the defendant-petitioner as to the acquisition of title by virtue of two registered documents in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party. In the pleadings of the defendant neither in his written statement nor in the appeal-memo as well as in the ground of this revisional application the title documents of the plaintiff has been challenged or objected from the side of the defendant-petitioner. In the memo of appeal the defendant-petitioner has totally waived his claim as agitated during hearing of this revisional application. The learned Advocate submits that the courts below prior to their observation and findings rightly assessed the evidence on records and in absence of any sort of illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate court the impugned judgment and decree cannot be interfered with. Two registered Kabala deeds (Exhibit 3, 4); by which the plaintiff acquired title in the suit property are not challenged from the side of the defendant and the learned courts below with regard to this rightly held that the plaintiff had title and interest in the suit property and the plaintiff also possessed the suit land but the defendant out of ill-motive dispossessed him. In fact; there is no evidence from the side of the defendant as to his alleged acquisition of title in 45 decimals of land in the suit holding by the vendor of the defendant-petitioner Bonde Ali who is the full-brother of the plaintiff-opposite party. Therefore; obviously the disputed ewajnania deed was a forged document which was not regally acted upon and the learned courts below concurrently with regard to this holding the view that the defendant-appellant-petitioner in fact did acquire any property by dint of his so called ewajnanur deed which is nothing but a paper transaction only. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the courts below at the time of disposal of the original suit and subsequent appeal hearing the arguments advanced from the side of the respective parties decided the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal on the basis of evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties on proper appreciation of law and inasmuch as there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice the Rule have got no merit to succeed. The learned Advocate Mr. Subrata Saha in his concluding submissons submits that this civil revision is not maintainable inasmuch as before filing of this rev isional application the defendant-appellant-petitioner preferred a review application before the lower appellate court which was awaiting for disposal on merit being No. Review Case No.02 of 2012 under Order XLV11 Rule 1/2 along with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in which the plaintiff-respondent filed a written objection. Before disposal of that Review Case the defendant-appellant out of ill-motive suppressing the actual facts practicing fraud upon the court have instituted this revisional application and as such the civil revision is not maintainable. 

 10. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocates of both sides having gone through the impugned judgment and decree along with the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court and the evidence on records as adduced from the sides of the respective parties with all other documentary evidence including connected papers on records it transpires that admittedly the suit property originally belonged to the father of the plaintiff and his brothers namely Mali Hossasin. It is also an admitted position that at the demise of Mali Hossain his one wife, eight sons and three daughters inherited the property left behind him. The brother of the plaintiff Bonde Ali by way of amicable partition among the heirs of Mali Hossain obtained .333/4 acres of land and the sisters obtained .111/4 acres of land in the disputed holding. It is the case of the plaintiff that Boucle Ali after getting .333/4 acres of land transferred 8% decimals of land from the suit two plots in the northern side by way of sub-kabala deed and thereby exhausted his share therein and the plaintiff use to borga possess the land of his sisters measuring an area of 111/4 decimals of land. The further case of the plaintiff to the original suit is such that his sister Jobeda Khatun by a sub-kabala deed dated 01.10.2000 transferred 10 decimals of land in his favour and the plaintiff by virtue of another sub-kabala deed dated 30.11.1998 acquired 25 decimals of land in the suit plots. It was contended from the side of the plaintiff in his pleadings that in the night following 08.10.2000 the defendant No.1 who is allegedly acquired the suit land from the defendant No. 2 Bonde Ali disposed him (plaintiff) from the suit property by erecting a tin-shed but therein. 

 11. The contrary case as it appears from the pleadings of the contesting defendant No.1 is such that his vendor Bonde Ali is the full-brother of the plaintiff who acquired the suit land through an amicable partition among the brothers and sisters who are the heirs of admitted original owner Mali Hossain. It was further contended from the side of the defendant-petitioner that there was a ewaj exchange between he and Bonde Ali in respect of the suit property on 19.09.2000 A.D. and possession was delivered in his favour by Bonde Ali on the very date and the defendant-appellant-petitioner after erecting his dwelling but use to possess the suit property since then. 

 14. It is a fact that, at the demise of the original owner, the plaintiff along with his 07(seven) brothers, 01(one) mother and 03(three) sisters inherited the property left behind their father Mali Hossain. Taking into consideration to that the learned trail court rightly held that the onus in proving the fact that one of the twelve heirs of Mali Hossain Bonde Ali obtained the total 45 decimals of land in the suit holding is required to be proved from the side of the defendant as it was his pleadings specific case. Inasmuch as it was the positive case of the defendant that the other brothers and sisters deprived of getting their shares the onus of proving the same lies upon the defendant under section 103 of the Evidence Act. 

 16. Apart from this; from the case records it is obvious to note that after disposal of the appeal being Title Appeal No.25 of 2005 by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.04.2012 by the learned Additional District Judge, Court, Kishoreganj the defendant-appellant preferred a Review Miscellaneous Case under Order XLV11 rule 1/2 along with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and this case was registered as case No.02 of 2012 "Review (Chhany)". In that case the plaintiff-respondent appeared and filed written objection. That Review Miscellaneous Case was preferred on 30.05.2012 and it's written objection was filed on 06.09.2012. While this Revisional Application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure has been preferred on 14.11.2012 before disposal of the aforesaid Review Miscellaneous Case No.02 of 2012 in which the defendant-appellant-petitioner has obtained the present Rule with an interim order of stay on 19.11.2012 and an order of status quo on 27.05.2014. 

 18. Be that as it may; it can be easily decided that fraud has vitiated the entire proceedings of this civil Rule, even then; for the interest of justice especially for complete justice I like to draw my attention over the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties in support of their respective cases. During trial of the original suit being Other Suit No.225 of 2000 the witness No.1 is the plaintiff himself who is Abdul Jabbar. The plaintiff in his testimony affirmed his respective pleadings as cited in his plaint and it is within his deposition that his father Mali Hossain purchased the suit land from the original owners Hem Chandra Dutta and 04 others prior to 50/60 years. Subsequently, at the demise of Mali Hossain his one wife, 08 sons and 03 daughters inherited his property. There has been an amicable partition among the brothers and sisters and the plaintiff acquired the suit land in his exclusive possession but one of his brother Bonde Ali out of ill-motive transferred the suit land in favour of the defendant No.1 namely Abdul Barik by a forged ewajnama deed by dint of which Abdul Barik on 08.10.2000 dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property. With regard to the documentary evidence produced from the side of the plaintiff I find that the respective S.A. Khatian No.786 has been marked as Exhibit-1 and the subsequent deeds has been marked as Exhibits-2, 3, 4 and 5. The disputed exchange deed being No.6203 dated 19.09.2000 is exhibit-2 from the side of the plaintiff. 

 23. On the other hand; D.W.1, Abdul Khaleque the defendant No.1 himself in his testimony categorically stated in the examination-in-chief that in the month of 'Ashur' the ewaj was held and from the date of ewaj he possess the suit land. He expressed his inability in his cross-examination to state the plot number of the suit land but admitted to the effect that the suit land originally belonged to the father of the plaintiff namely Mali Hossain and Mali Hossain died leaving behind 08(eight) sons, 03(three) daughters and 01(one) wife and there has been amicable partition among the sons and daughters of Mali Hossain. During cross-examination the defendant-appellant-petitioner frankly admitted at a stage that Bonde Ali did not obtain possession in his (D.W 1) exchanged land which was given by him (D.W.1) in favour of Bonde Ali in exchange of the suit land. The courts below giving much emphasis on this admission rightly arrived at a conclusive decision as to the nature of the disputed deed of exchange (Ewajnama) which admittedly did not take it's effect. In his (D.W.1)cross examination lie further admitted that he cannot say the Bengali date and year of his taking possession in the suit land and he also cannot say the Bengali date of his Ewaj deed. 

 26. With regard to the mistake done by the trial Judge during disposal of the original suit as to the framing of respective issue on possession and dispossession of the suit land our Apex Court in the case of Ismail Ullah being dead his heirs Baizidulluh and others —vs.- Sukumar Chandra Das, 1986 BLD(AD)251 held that the judge of the trial court can always amend the decree if there is a bonafide mistake done by him.

parties:
Syed Khaleduzzaman and others ----- Petitioners
VS
Moynul Hussain and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Mozibur Rahman Miah J: At the instance of the plaintiffs-petitioners, leave was granted and Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the Judgment and order dated 22-7-2015 passed by the learned District Judge, Sylhet in Civil Revision No. 4 of 2014 dismissing the revision and affirming the Judgment and order dated 19-1-2014 passed by the learned Assistant Judge (in-charge), Fenchugonj, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 13 of 1987 allowing the application filed for holding local investigation should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the further proceeding of Title Suit No. 13 of 1987 of the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Fenchugonj, Sylhet was stayed for a period of 6 (six) months which was lastly extended on 27-11-2016 for a further period of 3 (three) months. 

 That the present-petitioners as plaintiffs originally filed a suit in the year of 1953 as Title Suit No. No. 18 of 1953 for declaration of title, recovery of possession, as well as partition in the suit land as described to the schedules of the plaint. It has been stated by the learned counsel for the petitioners during hearing of the rule that, the said suit went up to the Hon'ble Appellate Division and during pendency of the execution proceedings so filed by the plaintiffs-petitioners, one of the defendants of the suit raised objection that, no notice has been served upon him and consequently, the said suit was sent back enabling the plaintiffs to sue afresh and eventually this petitioners as plaintiffs filed this suit being Title Suit No. 13 of 1987. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said Judgment and order, so passed by the learned District Judge, dated 22-7-2015, the plaintiffs as petitioners then filed this revisional application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure and this Court by order dated 15-11-2015 granted leave, issued Rule and stayed the further proceeding of Title Suit No. 13 of 1987. 

 13. It is undeniable that, the very suit was filed far back in the year 1953 and it was renumbered as Title Suit' No. 13 of 1987 and still continue and earlier application for holding local investigation has been disposed of in the year 2013 and soon after disposal of the earlier application, the petitioners filed another application on invoking the self-same provision of law, only exception is that, in the earlier application the petitioners did not ask for to ascertain the Jote and Taluk number. 

 19. The learned Assistant Judge, Fenchuganj, Sylhet is further directed to dispose of Title suit No. 13 of 1987 as soon as possible preferably within 6 (six) months from date.

parties:
Government of Bangladesh and others ------- Appellant
Vs.
Sultan Giasuddin and others ------- Respondent
full_judgment:
The respondent failed the above noted writ petition or the averments that their father Abdus Sobhan was a businessman who owned three cinema halls namely Diana, Meghna and Jamuna at Posthogola, Dhaka and a residential house situated at 46, Dinnath Road, P.S Sutrapur Dhaka. On the other hand one Sarwar Ahmed, after purchasing plot No. 5/3 pallabi, Mirpur, Dhaka from the Eastern Housing Limited, as shown in the lay out plan of Eastern Housing Estate vide registered deed No. 13866 dated 25.08.66, constructed at one storied building thereon in the year 1969 with the loan taken from house building finance Corporation, (HBFC), Dhaka; That Sarwar Ahmed, being in need of money, entered into an agreement with Abdus Sobhan on 7.10.1969 for sale of the above house along with the existing mortgage and HBFC Loan. Accordingly Sarwar Ahmed separately and jointly with Abdus Sobah filed two application to the HBFC for permission to materialized the said transfer of the above house along with the mortgage loan on 07.10.1969. The HBFC having agreed, accordingly permission to transfer the said house in favour of Abdul Sobhan through at registered tripartite sale deed, Abdus Sobhan by depositing money in the Dhaka treasury on 28.01.1970 purchased stamp and then tripartite sale deed was executed and registered on 28.04.1970 with registration No. 4733 dated 28.04.1970 at Dhaka Sadar Joint Register office. But during the liberation was the said original deed along with maximum original deeds having been destroyed, the above joint Register office failed to deliver the original deed to Abdus Sobhan. Fortunately the volume being kept intact and available with District Registrar Office, Dhaka a certified copy was obtained subsequently. However, Abdus Sobhan, made further construction in the said hose and was in peaceful possession of the same after liberation Abdus Sobhan having come to know from different quarters that the above hose has been enlisted in the list of abiding proper-ties, applied to the then sub-divisional officer (S.D.A) (South), Dhaka, for releasing has house form the list of abandoned properties whereupon the S.D.O (South) Dhaka directed his office to hold enquiry and on perusal of the inquiry report observed that Srawar Ahmed purchased the plot form the Eastern housing Limited in 1966 whereupon keeping the said property mortgaged to the HBFC he obtained loan and after constructing an one storied building he transferred the same to Abdus Sobhan by registered deed of sale in 1970 wherein HBFC is also a party. Thus it was held that ownership of Abdus Sobahan in the said house has been found to be proved. In his order dated 6.8.1973 the SDO held "he is Bengali and he did not abandon Bangladesh at the time of liberation of the country he was here after liberation. So, his house cannot be treated s an abandoned property under PO 16 of 1972 " it is further stated that he being an income tax assesses since long before, all along paying income tax under TIN number 19/SPL and also 4436 (Status Industry). He is also holder of Bangladeshi passport bearing no. B-00791 issued on 6.3.1973, which has been renewed from time to time. Apart from such report the HBFC, the mortgage, also issued a certificate on 24.12.1973 certifying that they issued notices upon Abdus Sobahn for payment of installments against the loan transferees in his name. it is further stated that on receipt of notice dated 30.10.1983 of the joint Survey Team, Ministry of works, Abdus Sobahan appeared before the said team long with documents for verification. He altos submitted a copy of the memo No, 857 MN III IN-300 79 dated 11.04.80 issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs which determined his national status and subsequently he also submitted more documents through registered post in support of his nationality. It is stated that though the possession of the above house was not ever taken over by the government, the Ministry of works by Notification no. SRO 364 L/86 published on 23.09.86, most illegally enlisted the said house in serial no. 14 in "Ka" list of the abandoned buildings. Thus Abdus Sobhan on 14.12.1986 filed an application before the chairman. Court of settlement, Dhaka praying for release of the above house from "Ka" list out during pendency of the same Abdus Sobhan died on 19.01.1998 in the Holy family Red Crescent Hospital, Dhaka and was buried at Azimpur Graveyard Dhaka on 20.01.1998. the writ petitioners being the heirs of Abdus Sobhan, become owners of the above house and got their name mutated in the office of eh Assistant Commissioner (Land) Tejgoan Circle vide Mutation Case No. 19615 dated 02.12.2001 and upon obtaining DCR paid ground rent along with other service charges, bills, holding taxes etc. they also filed application for substituting their name in place of late Abdus Sobhan before the court of Settlement which was kept in the record by the Court of settlement. Subsequently the Court of settlement registered the application of Abdus Sobhan as Case No, 156 of 2001 and by judgment and order dated 31.03.2003 dismissed the sad case. Finding no other efficacious remedy the writ petitioners filed writ petition No. 4176 of 2003 categorically asserting that inclusion of the said house in "Ka" list is illegal and the decision of the Court of Settlement is thus not sustainable in law and accordingly they obtained Rule Nisi. 

 4. The respondent No. 2 opposed the Rule by filling affidavit-in-opposition stating inter alia that the statements as contained in the writ petition are vague, false and fabricated and the writ petitioners have miserable failed to prove their right and title and also failed to produce the original deed being No. 4733 dated 28.04.1970; they also failed to prove their possession in the property in question. Hence, the rule Nisi is liable to be discharged. 

 6. Mr. Gautam Kumar Ray, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the Court of settlement on proper examination of all the papers and documents and after discussing the evidence of P.W.L: held they the original owners and his hers left this country before promulgation of the president's order No. 16 of 1972 and hence the whereabouts of the original owner of the house not being known to the Government, the said house was enlisted in the "Ka" list; Moreover the original purchase deed bearing No. 4733 dated 28.04.1970 has not been produced before the Court of settlement rather a certified copy of the aforesaid deed was submitted without proving the same lawful as the signature of the original owner of the property was not available in the said copy and accordingly rightly without considering these aspect fail in error in making the Rule absolute and as such the instant appeal should be allowed. 

 7. Mr. Aminul Haque, the learned senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that Sarwar Ahmed after purchasing the property in 1966 from the Eastern Housing Ltd. Constructed a one storied house upon on obtaining loan from the HBFC and thereafter transferred the same to Abdus Sobhan predecessor in interest of the respondent in 1970 vide registered sale deed along what the HBFC loan upon obtaining permission from the House Building Finance Corporation and thereafter continued paying installments of the corporation up on getting his name mutated in all offices and paying all rents, bills and service charge. After the death of Abdus Sobhan hi hairs, bill s charge and taxes. He also submits that the predecessor in interest of the respondents after getting information regarding enlistment of the said property in the abandoned property list filed an application before the sub-divisional officer, Dhaka, for releases of the same from the said list and sub-Divisional officer after holding a detailed enquiry was satisfied about the title, possession, citizenships as well as the where about of Abdus Sobhan, the owner of the property and as such referred the file to the Ministry of Works of necessary action to release the property from the list of abandoned properties. He next submits that the judgment of the court of settlement it's not a proper judgment as it did not consider the mandatory provisions as stipulated in the president order 16 of 1972 which is very much relevant for disposal of cases by neither the Court of Settlement nor it took into consideration the reports and the documents filed before it. It simply observed that the original sale deed was not filed but did not consider the certified copy of the same which is also admissible as evidence in absence or original registered deed. He finally submitted that through the property is listed in 'Ka' list out the survey team of the Department of Settlement, Government of Bangladesh itself found exclusive possession of the respondent in the house in question. Upon considering all these aspects the High Court Division rightly passed the Impugned judgment and hence the instant appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. It appears from the materials on record as well as the impugned judgment that Abdus Sobhan, the predecessor of the present respondent and subsequent to the death of said Abdus Sobhan the respondent are in possession of the case property. Admittedly Sarwar Ahmed was the original owner of the property in question who purchased the same in 1966 and transferred the property in question by registered deed of sale, in favor of Abdus Sobhan in 1970. It furthers appears that before the sale the said Sarwar Ahmed and Abdus Sobhan jointly applied to the house building Finance Corporation for materializing the transfer of the property in favor of Abdus Sobhan with HBFC Loan sand question upon he mortgagee where-upon the House Building Finance Corporation accorded permission and accordingly directed Abdus Sobhan to pay the installments regularly. Accordingly Abdus Sobhan got the property in question upon mutating the same in his name and started residing there upon constructing a three storied building obtaining gas, WASA and electricity connection and paying the bills thereof along with ground rents regularly. The possession of the property was never taken over by the government but when the Abdus Sobhan came to know about the enlistment of the same in the abandoned property list he immediately filed application to the sub Divisional Officer (DDC) for release of the same which upon holding detailed enquiry by order dated 28.12.1973 directed to release the property in question form the abandoned properly list and referred the file to the Ministry of Works for necessary action. 

 11. The only points as it appears from the judgment of the Court of Settlement for which it dismissed the prayer of the respondents, is that the claimants failed to produce the original sale deed executed in 1970 ignoring the face of destruction of the original registered deed of sale along with most of the original deeds from the registry office during the war of liberation. However, admittedly the respondents produced the certified copy of the registered sale deed (Annexure-D to the writ petition) before the Court of Settlement which also kept with the House Building Finance Corporation as security. The said document being a certified copy of the original deed of sale it is very much admissible as secondary evidence under section 65 of the Evidence Act. In the case of Abdul Hannan Vs ADC reported in 41 DLR(AD) 197 it has been held "the secondary evidence of a document is admissible in evidence" when a document is registered under the registration Act by the register and certified in accordance with law under section 60 of registration Act and accordingly incorporated in the volume, the certified copy of the same is sufficient to prove the genuineness of such registration in the absence of eh original documents unless the same is challenged and proved contrary to it. In the present case, the genuineness of the said certified copy of the registered sale deed has to been challenged by the government anywhere either before the court of settlement or before the High Court Division. 

 12. Under such circumstances and on consideration of the materials on record ii appears that the respondents have been able to prove their case before the High Court Division about the whereabouts of their father the owner of the house, his/their citizenship and their exclusive possession in the property in question since purchase and they are paying all charges, taxes and rents to the government my mutating their names. Moreover when the competent authority after holding proper inquiry found the predecessor of the respondents to the rightful owner in 1973 by virtue of the registered sale deed of 1970 and since then till date the present respondents are enjoying the possession of the same upon mutating their names in all the government records and sine the record of 1973 has never been challenged by the government or set aside by and appropriate authority and since in the recent Mohanagar Survey the name of the respondents have been correctly records as owners and possessors of the house in question and since they are paying installments to the House Building finance Corporation regularly, mere failure to produce the original deed of sale under no circumstances can take away the right of respondents.

parties:
Zarufa khatun and others.
Vs.
Md. Zainal Abedin and others
full_judgment:
Md. Rais Uddin, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.05.2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur in Title Appeal No.51 of 1991 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 13.3.1991 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge, Chandpur in Title Suit No.51 of 1990 dismissed the suit, should not be set-aside. 

 2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that Opposite-party No.1 as plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration that kabala executed and registered by the defendants Nos.4-6 in favour of the defendant Nos.1-3 being deed No.4602 dated 14.7.1987 is illegal, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff contending, inter-alia, that predecessor of Payia Gazi who was the owner of the land under Mouza No.48 Ullaskhar, previous Khatian No.19, measuring 8.09 acres comprised under present khatian No.19. The father of the plaintiff was the original owner of the suit land along with other land having his right, title and interest over the same by way of inheritance and purchase who by way of a "will" dated 14.05.1987 transferred 2.12 1/4 acres of land in favour of the plaintiff. The defendants Nos.4-6 who are the daughters of the ancestor, had no right, title and interest but they transferred .24 acres of land by way of execution of Saf Kabala deed registered on 14.7.1987 in favour of the defendants Nos.1-3 from their ancestral land. The plaintiff declared the suit land as belonged to him by way of "Will " and prayed for declaration of the deed dated 14.7.1987 is illegal, void, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 3. The defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filling joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that Payia Gazi their predecessor was the original owner over the land under disputed khatian No.19 and on his death the suit land devolved upon Sree Golap Jan the wife and 5 sons, namely, Alimuddin, Karimuddin, Rahimuddin, Imamuddin and Tukka Gazi. Golap Jan died leaving her above 5 sons. Tukka Gazi being unmarried died leaving his remaining 4(four) brothers as his heirs Imamuddin their predecessor having his right, title and interest over the suit land under Khatian No.19 by way of inheritance and over the land under Khatian No.6 of Dadia Para Mouza by way of purchase, died on 1380 B.S. leaving his wife Latifa Khatun, one son and Amir Jan, Bibi Jan, Ali Jan, Korpuler Nessa, Moiyar Bhanu and Berzi Jan his daughters as his heirs and legal representative and asserted that Imamuddin never did any Will " on 14.5.1987 and as lie died in 1380 B.S. and as such execution of " Will " on 14.5.1987 is absurd not believable. These contesting defendants under the same agnate purchased .24 decimals of land as described in the written statement specifying the nature character and position of the land from the defendant Nos.4-6 the full sisters of the plaintiff by way of a registered Saf Kabala deed being deed No.4602 dated 14.7.1987 and accordingly entailed with possession over the same by the defendant Nos.4-6 who have been in possession over their respective shares. The plaintiff intending to deprive his sisters fabricated an antedated and forged deed of "Will" after 17 years of the death of his father. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest over the suit land and as such the suit of the plaintiff should be dismissed. 

 12. On perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiff brought the suit challenging the sale deed dated 14.7.1987 executed by the defendant Nos.4-6 in favour of defendant Nos. 1-4 claiming that defendant Nos.4-6 had no right, title to sale the suit land because the original owner of the land namely, lmanuddin father of plaintiff and defendant Nos. 4-6 had already executed " Will " in the year 1972 infavour of plaintiff which was registered on 14.5.1987 measuring 2.12 1/2 acres of land and the defendants transferred the same by a sale deed dated 14.7.1987. 

 "S.A. and R.S. records were not an evidence of title and that a registered document would prevail upon the records of rights and that the registered document would remain in enforce unless the same was cancelled by an appropriate civil Court." 

 26. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The judgment and decree of the Appellate court in Title Appeal No.51 of 1991 is hereby affirmed. There will be no order as to costs.

full_judgment:
6. After hearing, learned Joint District Judge and District Delegate dismissed the case by holding that the 'Will' in question has been written in simple green paper and signature of PW.2 is not identical with her signature in the He further held that another witness of the 'Will' namely Koly has not been examined as witness. Learned District Delegate further held that documents of title of Shova Rani Roy the original owner was not produced and the 'Will' is not believable. 

 7. At the time of hearing of the appeal, the appellant filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for taking additional evidence in respect of deed of title dated 26.4.1984, 18.2.1968 annexing photocopies of those documents as Annexure A and A-1 . 

 8. Mr. S.N. Goswami, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that in a Probate case the Court is required only to consider whether the 'Will' was executed by the testator and it was attested by the witnesses. The Court need not decide question relating to title of the property. Mr. Goswami further contends that out of two witnesses mentioned in the 'Will' Sreemoti Chandana deposed as PW.2 who proved the execution of the 'Will'. He further submits that another witness of the 'Will' namely Koly was a declarant in the substantive application where she put her signature. 

 9. Learned Advocate in support of his submissions referred the case of Saktirani Ghosh V. Gautam Ghosh reported in AIR 1979 NOC 46 (CAL.) wherein the following passage is relevant: "Under the law of Evidence one of the attesting witnesses' evidence is sufficient to prove the Will: as such non-calling of the doctor who is the other attesting witness could not be a ground for withholding the grant of probate of Will" He also referred the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Comilla -Vs-Arun Kumar Chakraborty and others reported in 9 BLT(HCD) 192 wherein it has been stated that "In a Probate case, the Court is required only to consider whether the Will was duly executed by the testator and it was attested by witnesses. The Court cannot go into and decide any question relating to title in the disputed property." 

 12. In a Probate case the Court is required to consider whether the 'Will' is executed by the testator and it was attested by the witnesses. The Court is not required to consider to decide question of title. 

 13. Upon perusal of the Annexures the documents of title submitted by the appellant's, which are registered instruments we found chain of title in favour of Shova Rani Roy.

parties:
Ruhul Amin (Md) and others ------ Defendant-Appellant-Petitioners 
Vs.
Mustafizur Rahman and others ------ Plaintiff-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 11-6-2012 and 21-6-2012 respectively passed by the learned District Judge, Noakhali in Title Appeal No. 114 of 2011 disallowing the appeal by upholding the judgment and decree dated 31-10-2011 and 3-11-2011 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Chatkhil in Title Suit No.124 of 2006 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be; stated thus, the present opposite party No.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted the Title Suit No.124 of 2006 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Chatkhil, Noakhali against the present petitioners and opposite parties No.3-40 impleading them as defendants praying for declaration of title and further declaration that the deed of exchange Nos. 22 and 23 dated 2-1-1971 are forged, fraudulent, collusive and not acted upon contending infer alia, that the suit land appertaining to CS khatian No.359 corresponding to SA khatian No.372 measuring an area of 77 decimals of land in plot No.1735 under Mouza Topga originally belonged to one Yousuf Mollah who died leaving behind three daughters namely Syedunnessa, Rubitunnessa and Faridunnessa. Yousuf Mollah had another daughter namely Khairunnessa who died before him. The SA khatian was prepared in the name of Yousuf Mollah. He executed a waqf deed being No.782 dated 4-3-1916 in the name of his aforesaid three daughters and one grandson namely Ahmed Ullah. Saydunncssa died leaving behind three sons Waziullah, Aman Ullah, Fazley Rahman and one daughter Fatema Begum. By amicable settlement, Syedunnessa got 77 decimals of land of suit plot No.1735 and at the demise of Syedunnessa her property was amicably settled among her heirs and the suit plot No.1735 fallen into the saham of Waziulla, who died leaving behind two sons namely Mustafizur Rahman and Enaytur Rahman and they were owning and possessing the same. The son of Syedunnessa namely Fazlur Rahman died leaving, three sons namely Abdul Momen, Abdul Matin and Harunur Rashid. Abdul Matin died leaving behind two sons Mizanur Rahman and Muksudur Rahrrlan and two daughters namely Noorjahan Begum and Shahinur Begum. The son of Syedunnessa namely Amanullah died leaving behind three sons namely Mostafa, Helal Uddin, Zahiruddin and two daughters Shefali Begum and Shetera Begum. Rabitunnessa died leaving one son Aman Ullah and one daughter Halima Begum. That the son Faridunnessa Abdul Fattah died leaving behind one son Tariqul Islam and two daughters Kamrun Nahar, Ohidun Nahar. The son of Faridunnessa namely Abdur Rahim died leaving one son Abul Khair and one daughter Ajkarnessa and in this way the plaintiffs are the heirs of Waziullah, the son of Syedunnessa. The other heirs of Syedunnessa i.e, the defendant's No. 34-51 and Waziullah got 77 decimals of land in suit plot No.1735. In the suit land the defendants had no right, title and possession but they are claiming the suit land by way of collusive exchange deeds. Further case of the plaintiffs is such that after getting the certified copy of the deeds, they came to know that one Mobarakullah and Nurul Amin being the1st party exchanged the suit land with one ABM Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan showing him, in party but in fact the 1st party had no right, title and possession in the land of exchange it appears from the certified copy of the deed that Takdir Hossain Chowdhury, son of Alhaj Ramjan Ali Miazi is the recipient of the said deed and not Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan, son of Ator Ali. On the basis of the aforesaid collusive deed of exchange the defendants denied the title of the plaintiffs which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendants No.2, 4, 6, 18-21, 25, 26, 28 and 32 in short is thus, that the suit land is situated at Mouza-Topga under Police Station-Ramganj of District Noakhali which is recorded in CS khatian No.359, MRR No.372,plot No.1735 and total area 77 decimals out of38.50 acres of land. Further case of the contesting defendants is such that 1 anna, 6 gandas, 2 koras, 2 krantis were recorded in the name of Abdur Rashid and 2 annas, 13 gandas, 1kara, 1 kranti was recorded in the name of Abdul Latif and the rest 12 annas was recorded in the name of Yusuf Mollah. That non suited land of the said khatian of plot No.1179 measuring an area of 26 decimals was recorded in the name of Abdur Rashid and plot No.1180 comprising an area of 24 decimals was recorded in. the name of Yusuf Mollah and in plot No.1201 comprising an area of 76 decimals, In plot No.1306 an area of 19 decimals, in plot No.1316 an area of 42 decimals arid in plot No.1318 an area of 62 decimals was recorded in the name of Yusuf Mollah and the suit plot No.1735 comprising an area of 76 decimals of land was recorded in the name of Yusuf Mollah and thus Yusuf Mollah become the owner of 2.38 acres of land in all. Subsequently, Yusuf Mollah died leaving behind four daughters namely Jamila Khatun @ Khairunnessa, Syedunnessa, Rahimunnessa and Faridunnessa. Jamila Khatun @ Khairunnessa was married with one Raja Mia and she was living with her husband. Those other three daughters of Yusuf Mollah got married but they use to live in their father's residence. At the time of preparation of MR Rkhatian No.372 the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of two daughters and legal heirs of one daughter omitting the name of Jamila @ Khairunnessa. By amicable settlement Jamila Khatun @ Khairunnessa got 38.50 acres of the suit land and for such wrong record, the right of Jamila Khatun @ Khairunnessa was extinguished. Jamila Khatun died leaving behind two sons Mobarakullah and Siddiqullah. Siddiqullah died leaving behind one son Nurul Amin. Mobarakullah and Nurul Amin have been owning and possessing 38.50 acres of land of suit plot No.1735 for about 40 years. Thereafter, on 2-1-1971 they made two exchange deeds being No. 22 and 23 with one ABM Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan and they made over possession of the suit land to Takdir Hossain. Thereafter Takdir Hossain died leaving behind the defendants No. 25-12 who had been owning and possessing the suit land for about 32 years. The plaintiffs had no right, title, possession in the suit land in any manner. Besides this, there exist a road to the eastern side of the suit plot which include 41/2decimals of land and 34 decimals was owned and possessed by defendants No.25-32 and in the recent survey khatian No.747, Plot No. 6033 was recorded in the names of defendants No.25-32. The plaintiffs did not file any objection under sections 30/31 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1955. The plaintiffs had no right, title and possession in the suit land. The plaintiffs have no locus standi to file the suit. 

 4. The learned trial court i.e. the Assistant Judge, Chatkhil during trial of the original suit after examining witnesses from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 31-10-2011. Being aggrieved, the defendants preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 114 of 2011 in the court of earned District Judge, Noakhali and the learned District Judge, by the impugned judgment and decree dated 11-6-2012 disallowed the appeal' affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the appellate court below during passing the impugned judgment and decree violated the provisions laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. There is no assessment of evidence and appreciation of law in its true perspective. The learned Advocate submits that the trial court as well as the appellate court during deciding the fate of the suit and its subsequent appeal misconstrued the actual position of law and without proper sifting of evidence arrived at an erroneous finding resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. During trial of the original suit the plaintiff-opposite parties have utterly failed to discharge their onus in proving their case by any dependable evidence and the evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiffs are not trustworthy, rather they have falsified the case of the plaintiffs on title and possession. The learned Advocate submits that the title documents of the defendants i.e. the deeds of exchange are more than 30 years old and its proper custody inasmuch as was proved, under section 90 of the Evidence Act it is presumed to, be correct. In this context; the learned Advocate cited several decisions of our Apex Court. 

 8. The learned counsel on behalf of the petitioners during his argument submits that the plaintiffs in their testimony admits that the record of right stands recorded in the name of the defendants. The so called possession witnesses of the plaintiffs are not competent, credible, disinterested and trustworthy. The witness No.1 is the plaintiffs No.1 himself and the witnesses No.2-4 are the possession Witnesses of the plaintiffs who has totally failed to establish the plaintiff's possession, right and title over the suit land. On the contrary the defendants in support of their case have adduced 5(five) witnesses who have successfully proved the case of the defendants as stated within the contents of their pleadings. All the title documents of the defendants have been marked as Exhibits after proof without objection and there are no discussions and findings of the courts below on the said documents which has been proved and marked as Exhibits without objection. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the defendants in respect of the suit land mutated their names and have been paying rents regularly to the government. In respect of 'Ga' schedule land of the plaint the plaintiffs are claiming title but the land as described in that schedule is without specification and, as such, under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act the plaintiff's suit is barred. The deeds of exchange which has been challenged from the side of the plaintiffs in the suit were not challenged earlier and as a result of that under Article 91 of the Limitation Act as within three years from the date of the documents those were not challenged, the plaintiff's claim is barred by limitation. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument  advanced from the side of the learned Advocate for the petitioners and submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and Its subsequent appeal after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law decided all the matters-in-issue concurrently in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants. The learned Advocate further submits that there is no illegality or irregularity and no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned Advocate also submits that the deeds of exchange which are the basic documents of the defendants are forged, created and not acted upon which would be apparent from the name of the executant of the deed and from the deposition of the witness No. 1 of the defendants and thus it is clear that the executant is a fictitious person. The certified copy of the deed being No. 3039 has been falsified from the defendant Md Zahangir Hossain who has stated that Yousuf Mollah left behind four daughters namely Khairunnessa @ Jamila, Syedunnessa, Rabidunnessa and Farid-un-nessa. He further states that Khairunnessa @ Jamila lived with her husband Raja Miah separately and the MRR Khatian was prepared omitting her name but the recent khatian has been prepared in the name of his brother Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan. From the face of the documents it appears that not Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan but one Takdir Hossain Chowdhury, son of Alhaj Ramjan Ali Miazi is the recipient of the deed No.3039 which has been marked as Exhibit-4 and the matter has been properly addressed by the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the courts below in their observation and findings concurrently decided that the deeds of exchange are forged, collusive and manipulated. The learned Court have cited some reasons within the findings which are consistent with the evidence on records and, as such, there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. 

 11. On perusal of the case records it transpires that admittedly the suit land originally belonged to one Yousuf Mollah and it is the case of the plaintiffs that Yousuf Mollah died leaving behind his three daughters. His another daughter died during his life time leaving one son Ahmed Ullah and Vis-a-vis it was contended from the side of the defendants that at the demise of Yousuf Mollah his four daughters namely Khairunnessa @ Jamila, Syedunnessa, Rabidunnessa and Faridunnessa inherited the property left, behind by Yousuf Mollah. Khairunnessa married with one Raja Miah and by way of amicable settlement among the heirs in all 38 and 1/2 decimals of land in plot No.1735 lies in the saham of Khairunnessa @ Jamila who died leaving two sons Siddiqullah and Mobarakullah. 

 13. I have come across the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties that to substantiate the plaintiff's case they have adduced four witnesses. The witness No. 1 is the plaintiff No.1 himself Md Mostafizur Rahman. The plaintiff No. 1 in his testimony admits at a stage that the deeds of exchange are of more than 38/39 years and the recent survey was completed in their area in the year 1990-91 and the suit land of SA plot No.1735 has been recorded in recent survey as plot No.6033 and in 41/2 decimals of land of the suit plot there is a road by which the villagers move. He also admits that in the recent settlement plot No.6033, 34 decimals, of land have been included in field survey khatian No.2019 and in DP khatian No.787 which has been prepared in the name of the defendant's father and against that they did not file any case under sections 30/31 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In respect of the disputed exchange deeds the plaintiff No.1 states that his father died in the year 1993 and the deeds were executed and registered in the year 1971. During the life time of his father he did not file any case and after 40 years of the deeds they have 'instituted the original suit. Admittedly, the plaintiffs have failed to produce any Rent Receipt showing payment of rent in respect of the suit land and as regard their possession the witnesses who deposed as witness Nos. 2,3,4 and 5 tried to establish the case of the plaintiffs but from the examination-in-chief of these witnesses it is apparent from the face of the papers that the witnesses have failed to describe the actual identity of the suit land including its specification and as regard boundary they have totally failed to state anything. On the other hand, the defendants in support of their case have adduced five witnesses and among them DW1 is the defendant No.26 who tried to corroborate their pleading in his testimony. It is to be noticed that the established principle of civil law is such that it is the plaintiffs who in order to obtain a decree in their favour shall have to discharge their onus in proving their case, but on critical analysis of evidence I find that in respect of title and possession of the plaintiffs they have totally failed to prove their case by any tangible evidence and the evidence led from their side is not at all trustworthy, credible and competent. 

 14. Besides this, the proposition of law is such that under section 90 of the Evidence Act if a document is 30 years old or more than that, be produced from. a proper custody is presumed to have been signed and written by the person whose signature and writings are found and to have been executed and attested duly. No proof of any of these facts is required and the document, if it is thirty years old or more will prove itself provided it is produced from proper custody. In this context, the learned Advocate of the petitioners cited two decisions of our Apex Court passed in the case of Syed Abdul Haque vs Surendra Nath Majumder reported in 59 DLR (AD) 111 and the decision given in the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Pabnavs Md Reazuddin Pk. reported in 8 BLT (AD) 185 = 5 BLC (AD) 76 law enjoins that without establishing the plaintiff's own title and possession they are not entitled to challenge any other deeds by way of simple declaration within the ambit of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and in this context a decision is referred from the petitioner's side of our Appellate Division in the case of Ratan Chandra Dey vs Jinnator Nahar reported in 2XP (AD) 313. Apart from this, under the purview of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act with regard to a suit for declaration of title to an unspecified portion of land a decision is referred from the side of the petitioners of our Apex Court reported in 2XP (AD) 68 and the decision given by this Court in the case of Bashiur Rahman Biswas vs Md Hanif Ali Biswas reported in 21 BLD 89 = 7 BLC186. 

 15. Having regard to the decisions referred to above I may not be out of place to advert the provisions laid down in Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure regarding the specification and identification of the suit land which is badly required for having a declaration of title. The description of the land must be specific with its boundary and if it is found that the land described in the schedule of the plaint suffers from any vagueness or un-specification the plaintiff must suffer. Furthermore, the plaintiffs in order to succeed must establish their own case by credible evidence and weakness of the defendants is no ground for awarding a decree in favour of the plaintiffs. 

 16. In the instant case; as I have already referred to above, that in respect of a particular portion or land described in schedule 'ga' of the plaint the plaintiffs have sought for a declaration of title and the witnesses have totally failed to discharge their onus in proving the respective case of the plaintiffs as to their alleged possession and identification of the land. Besides this, having gone through the impugned judgment and decree it is evident to note that the lower appellate court i.e. the learned District Judge, Noakhali at the time of disposal of the appeal on merit have utterly failed to assess the evidence on records and there is no discussion of evidence and no sifting of the same in its true perspective. Under the ambit of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is the incumbent duty upon the appellate court below while affirming or reversing the judgment of the trial court that, the appellate court shall state the reasons for the decision after proper evaluation and assessment of evidence on records. Our Apex Court in the case of Hajarilal Mondal vs Md Mozaffor Bepari reported in 8 BLC (AD) 77 held that it is the principle of law that the lower appellate court being the final court of fact will have to discuss and re-assess the evidence on records independently while either reversing or affirming the findings of the trial court. But in the instant case as I have cited above that the learned District Judge have totally failed to scan the evidence on records by his discussion and evaluation of both oral and documentary evidence. 

 17. Before parting, however, I like to advert that with regard to the name of 'Takdir Hossain Bhuiyan' and 'Takdir Hossain Chowdhury' as it appears meanwhile that the proposition of law made herein above has imposed legal embargo upon the plaintiffs in getting the relief as prayed for it is needless to discuss more inasmuch as it is immaterial at this stage. Be that as it may, I find that the plaintiffs to the suit in order to succeed must have to establish their case and to stand on their own legs. But analyzing the evidence led from their side it is crystal clear that the plaintiffs have totally failed to discharge their onus in proving their right, title, interest and possession over the suit land by adducing credible, cogent, tangible evidence which can be treated trustworthy. 

 19. In the result, the Rule having much merit is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 11-6-2012 and 21-6-2012 respectively passed by the learned District Judge, Noakhali in Title Appeal No. 114 of 2011 disallowing the appeal by upholding the judgment and decree dated 31-10-2011 and.3-11-2011 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Chatkhil in Title Suit No. 124 of 2006 is hereby set-aside. The original suit be dismissed on contest without cost.

parties:
Jahangir (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md Altaf Hossain and others ------ Opposite Parties

Amena Khatun and other ------ Plaintiffs-Appellants
VS
Hem Chandra Ray and others ------ Defendants-Respondents
full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury J: This appeal, at the instance of the plaintiffs as appellants, is directed against the judgment and decree dated November 28-11-1993 passed in Title Suit No. 6 of 1986 by the learned Subordinate, Judge, Jessore. 

 2. Facts in short, out of which this appeal has arisen are that the appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 6 of 1986 before the Subordinate Judge, Jessore impleading the respondents as defendants seeking a decree for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and in the alternative a saham of 0.44 acres of land by way of partition. 

 3. The case of the plaintiffs in short, are that the suit land originally belonged to Balu Mollah as tenant under Erfan Mollah, and it was recorded in the name of Balu Mollah under CS Khatian No. 35; Balu Mollah having been in possession in exercise in his title therein, died leaving behind One son Aftab Mollah and a daughter Bindhu Bibi as his heirs. Thereafter, Aftab Mollah and Bindhu Bibi having been in possession and enjoyment of the suit land in exercise of their mourosui maliki right executed a mortgage deed on 20-1-1932 in favour of Satiya Charan and the mortgage was subsequently redeemed. Thereafter, Aftab Mollah and Bindhu Bibi jointly possessed the suit land. Subsequently, Aftab Mollah expressed his willingness to lease out 16½ decimals of land from plot No. 189(359) and one Hari Mohan was engaged to write the patta; said Hari Mohan collusively entered 0.27 acres of land of plot No. 187 and 0.39 acres of plot No. 190 in the registered patta deed dated 26-9-1940, behind the back of its executant Aftab Mollah; thereafter Aftab Mollah executed another patta on 6-3-1941 wherein it was disclosed that the patta registered on 26-9-1940 was not acted upon as there were mistakes; subsequently in the year 1943 Aftab Mollah died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs; the registered patta dated 26-9-1940 therefore did not confer any title in respect of the suit land in favour of Hari Mohan. When Bindhu Bibi daughter of Aftab Mollah found it difficult to retain her property she had to bring Title Suit No. 35 of 1953 before the Munsif, 3rd Court, Jessore impleading Hari Mohan Roy, Hari Dasi and others as defendants where Bindhu Bibi got a contested decree and in that suit the patta dated 26-9-1910 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Dasi was found as not sustainable in law. 

 39. When the plaintiffs had gone for cutting Segun tree from the suit land they were objected to by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and at that stage the plaintiffs for the first time came to know that the record of right in respect of the suit land had been prepared wrongly in favour of the father of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 although the defendants had no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land consequently the instant suit was brought for declaration of their title by the plaintiffs and for recovery of khas possession and in the alternative the plaintiffs, prayed for a sham to the extent of 0.44 acres in the suit land by partition in the form of preliminary decree. The plaintiffs also prayed for declaration that the patta dated 6-9-1940 in favour of Hari Mohan Roy executed by Aftab Mollah is null and void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and the added defendant 3(Ka) entered appearance in the suit upon filing two separate written statements; in the written statement filed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 they denied the material allegations made in the plaint stating inter alia that the suit land along with other lands originally belonged to Balu Mollah and it was recorded in CS khatian No. 35 correctly who having been in possession and enjoyment of the suit land along with other lands, died leaving behind his only son Aftab Mollah and only daughter Bindu Bibi as his heirs. Aftab Mollah being in possession of the suit land transferred 0.66 acres of land at a salami of Taka 150 fixing 2.25 anas yearly rent upon executing a registered patta dated 26-9-1940 in favour of Hari Dasi the mother of defendant Nos.1 and 2, an area of 16½ decimals of land appertaining to plot No.189 and plot No. 356 not covered by suit land was also transferred in favour of Hari Mohan Roy the father of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by another registered patta dated 6-3-41 executed by Aftab Mollah and handed over possession where the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 got possession by constructing house thereof; the patta executed by Aftab Mollah, in 1941 in favour of the father of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 being registered deed No. 194 contains an averment that patta dated 6-9-1940 being a mistaken one it was not acted upon but such an averment made by Aftab Mollah in his subsequent patta of 1941 was illegal and beyond authority; Aftab Mollah and his wife admitted the predecessor of the answering defendants as tenant upon receipt of rent from them. The answering defendants have been residing in the said house constructed by their father. The answering defendants have been in possession and enjoyment of the suit hind from the time of their predecessor right from the year 1940 therefore a title by adverse possession has also accrued in their favour. The answering defendant Nos. 1 and 2 also disclosed in the written statement that they have sold out 0.11-3/4 acres of land in favour of Gyanodabala by a registered kabala and had handed over possession where, on the death of Gyanodabala, her son has been in possession thereof. 

 7. In course of trial of the suit the plaintiffs examined two witnesses of them Jarina Khatun was examined a PW 1 and Rakib Mollah was also examined as PW 2. On the other hand, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 examined six witnesses on their behalf while the defendant No. 3(ka) examined one Guru Das as DW 1 in support of his case.
