Upon conclusion of the trial the learned Joint District Judge by his judgment and decree dated 28-11-1993 dismissed the suit. 

 9. Mr Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants has taken us through the materials on record including the impugned judgment as also the exhibits produced from both sides and submits that in the instant appeal it is an admitted position that the suit land along with other land originally belonged to one Valu Mollah and it was rightly recorded in CS khatian No.35, CS plot No.187 and 190 SA khatian No.46 and 43 SA plot Nos.209 and 210 under the Mouza Ghope, PS Kotwali, District Jessore and Valu Mollah having been in possession and enjoyment of the suit land along with other lands, died leaving behind his only son Aftab Mollah and only daughter Bindhu Bibi as his legal heirs who having been in possession and enjoyment of the land left behind by their father Aftab Mollah offered to lease out 16½ decimals of land from non suited plot Nos. 189/359 to one Hari Mohan Roy the father of respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and on 26-9-1940 a collusive deed of patta was purported to have been executed and registered on 26-4-1940 in favour or Hari Dasi Roy by Aftab Mollah and in the said deed of patta 0.66 acres of land from suit plots were shown to have been registered as a result in the following year i.e. on 6-3-1941 Aftab Mollah executed another deed of patta in favour of Hari Mohan Roy in respect of 16½ decimals of land from non suited CS plot No. 189/359 with an averment that the deed of patta date 26-4-1940 in favour of Hari Dasi Roy was not acted upon because errors were detected therein; about 3 years later in 1943 Aftab Mollah died leaving behind a widow Akarjan and three minor daughters who are the appellants before this court as his legal heirs. 

 10. Mr Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, also submits that in the year 1953 Bindhu Bibi instituted Title Suit No. 35 of 1053 impleading Hari Dasi Roy and Hari Mohan Roy as defendant Nos. 1 and 2 seeking a decree for partition and that suit was decreed on contest and the plaintiff Bindi Bibi was allotted a saham to the extent of 33 decimals of land. The plaintiffs used to enjoy and possess the suit land by enjoying usufructs there from but the defendants raised claim of the suit land on the basis of the aforesaid patta and subsequent record of right prepared in their names and on 21-3-1982 the plaintiffs were resisted to cut segun trees from the suit land by the defendants and finally on 12-1-1989 the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit land by the defendants, therefore, the suit was brought as aforesaid. 

 15. Mr Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan submits further that a case of title by adverse possession and the case on the basis of document cannot be claimed simultaneously as in the instant case. In substantiating his submission the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Push pa Rani Saha Podder vs Rash Mohan Saha being dead his heirs Kartick Chowdhury Saha reported in 26 BLD (AD) 50 

 16. Mr. Bhuiyan also submits that the claim of title by adverse possession was neither specifically pleaded nor proved by the defendants and no issue was framed to that effect either, nonetheless the learned Joint District Judge, conferred the title on the plaintiffs by a gratuitous finding of adverse possession in their favour which is not sustainable. In this connection he placed reliance in the case of Mahaprabhu Ram vs Gopal Ram reported in 42 DLR (AD) 154 and the case of 1 Hazera Begum vs Roushan Ara Begum reported in 39 DLR (AD) 22, the case of Mst Ghulani Hain vs Muhammad Waris Khan reported in 10 DLR (FC) 174 and Tajuddin vs Moktar Ahmed reported in 1991 BLD (AD) 44. It is also submitted by Mr Bhuiyan that SA record prepared in the name of the defendants which has got no presumptive value of correctness in as much as it has no basis as such mere preparation of SA khantian in their names or payment of rent by them does not create any title in favour of the defendants. In this connection the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Halima Begum vs Syed Ahmed reported in 21 DLR 854. The case of Chand Mali vs Md Hossain All being his heirs 1(ka) Md Sekander Ali reported in 3 BLC 364 and the case of Lal Mia being dead his heirs Momena Khatun vs Haji Md Ibrahim reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61. 

 17. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellant that mere nonpayment of rent by the plaintiffs does not extinguish or affect their title to the suit land. In this connection the learned Advocate for the petitioner placed reliance in the case of Abdur Noor vs Aziruddin reported in 21 BLT (AD) 161. 

 18. Mr Bhuiyan submits further that the finding of fact arrived at by the learned Munsif in Title Suit No.35 of 1953 to the effect that the claim of the parents of defendant Nos.1 and 2 by patta of 1940 and 1941 were bad in law, till subsist since no appeal or cross-appeal or revision was filed against the said judgment and decree is such the said judgment is admissible in evidence in the instant case and binding upon the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 within the meaning of section 43 of the Evidence Act and it will also operate as resjudicata against them since their parents were party to that suit. In this connection the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Nasim All vs Safina Bibi reported in 1988 BLD 493. 

 23. The learned Advocate for the respondents submits further that in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954, Exhibit-Ga was found to be bad in law only but it was not declared to be invalid. Therefore, the finding with respect to Exhibit-Ga in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 cannot raise the issue of resjudicata in the instant suit. 

 24. The learned Advocate for the respondents submits furt that possession under mistaken or invalid title is effective to extinguish owner's title. The plaintiffs did not claim their title by adverse possession is not enough to deny the relief lie is entitled to. In substantiating his submission the learned advocate placed reliance in the case of Sadak Ali vs Suruj Ali, reported in 7 DLR 95. 

 25. The learned Advocate for the respondent submits lastly that the apparent observation in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 with respect to Exhibit to the effect that the same is bad in law by the trial court was not given by framing any issue to that effect, therefore, such observation having no binding effect on any person whatsoever therefore does not raise any question of res judicata in the instant suit. 

 26. We have heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the materials on record including the depositions of the witnesses and the documents exhibited from both sides wherefrom it transpires that the main issue involved in this appeal as to whether patta dated 26-9-1940 purported to have been executed by Aftab Mollah one of the admitted original owner of the suit land in favour Hari Dasi Roy, Exhibit-Ga had divested Aftab Mollah of his title to the properties covered by the said patta or not, if the answer is in the affirmative in that case, case of the plaintiffs must fail. But if the answer is in the negative in that case, the plaintiffs must succeed, therefore, having concentrated our full attention to the said Exhibit-Ga, we find that Title Suit No.35 of 1954 (wrongly written as 1953 in some places) was instituted before the 3rd Court of Munsif, Jessore by Bindhu Bibi as plaintiff impleading Hari Mohan Roy and Hari Dasi Roy as main defendant Nos. 1 and 2 respectively along with 5 others as defendants seeking a decree for declaration of plaintiffs title to the extent of 5 annas 4 pai share in the suit land and possession therein by partition and in the said suit one of the six issues No. 5 was to the effect as under:— 

 "Has the plaintiff her alleged right title and interest in the land in suit." 

 27. It may be pointed out that Bindhu Bibi is the only daughter of Valu Mollah, the admitted original owner of the suit land, which was also averred in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954. Of course, Bindhu Bibi had only one brother named Aftab Mollah and this part of the case is also admitted by both the parties. 

 28. Having gone through the judgment delivered in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 carefully, we find that in that suit too Hari Mohan Roy and Hari Dasi Roy claimed their title in the suit land as defendants on the basis of two pattas one dated 26-9-1940 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Had Dasi Roy and the other dated 06-3-41 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Mohan Roy and in deciding the title the plaintiffs the learned Munsif clearly observed as under:— 

 31. In deciding the plaintiff’s title in the said Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 the learned Munsif arrived at a definite finding 10 the effect:— 

 32. We have also found that in the said Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 the validity of the two pattas, one in favour of Hari Mohan Roy dated 26-4-40 and other dated 6-3-1941 Exhibit-A and A(1) respectively in that suit were very much in issue before the learned Munsif and having considered the submission from both sides and upon consideration of the evidence on record available before him the learned Munsif arrived at a definite finding as quoted above. Therefore, findings in respect of both the two documents namely the aforesaid two pattas are very much binding upon the parties, involved in that suit, more particularly when it is an admitted position that the said judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 was not challenged before any higher forum and in such view of the matter we have no hesitation to hold that the finding with respect to patta dated 26-9-40 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Dasi Roy as arrived in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 operate as res judicata , therefore, no finding to the contrary with respect to the said document Exhibit-Ga in this appeal namely patta dated 26-9-40 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Dasi Roy is possible, therefore, it can be safely held that the Exhibit-Ga did not confer any title in favour of Hari Dasi Roy or in other words divested Aftab Mollah of his title in respect of the land covered by the same. 

 are based on misreading and misconstruction of evidence of PWs 1 and 2 while the evidence on the point of resjudicata is totally misconceived and based on total misconstruction of the pleadings of the parties rather in this connection we have found the finding with respect to Exhibit-Ga arrived at by the learned Munsif in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 (wrongly written as 1953) operates as resjudicata on a finding to the contrary in respect of Exhibit-Ga in the present suit and the finding of the learned Munsif in the previous suit in this respect stands as final by operation of law. 

 38. Defendants, witnesses are six in number of them DW 1 Hem Chandra Roy who is defendant No. 1, DW 2 Md Shahabuddin, DW 3 Adiluddin Bepari, DW 4 Md Motiar Rahman, DW 5 Noban Ali and DW 6 Eakub Ali Biswas they have deposed in the case and supported the defendants story therein but for our purpose we do not feel it necessary to discuss the same elaborately in view of our finding to the effect that the Exhibit-Ga the patta dated 26-9-40 was never acted upon, therefore, it had not conferred any title either to Hari Dasi or her successor the defendants. On the contrary we have also noticed that by the patta dated Exhibit-Ga(1) executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Mohan Roy dated 8-3-41 relates to the same land beyond the suit land where the defendants claimed to have been in possession by erecting their homestead and the said land being adjacent to the suit land. The learned Joint District Judge got himself confused referring to different statements made by the witnesses and consequently dismissed the suit on the point of limitation holding to the effect that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession within 12 years from the date of institution of the suit. Therefore, the findings of the trial court with respect thereto are not at all sustainable in law members of his family moreover those rent receipts tax receipts do not attract the suit land as no specification of land is available therein. It may also be pointed out that the defendants took a duel plea in their pleading in a casual way one is that they claim title on the basis of patta dated 26-9-40 and the other one for adverse possession. The learned Joint District Judge dismissed the suit and arrived at a conclusion that the defendants acquired title both on the basis of their pattas as well as by adverse possession, which is not sustainable in law, in view of the principle of law enunciated in 26 BLD (AD) 50 to the effect that case of title by adverse possession and a case of title on the basis of document cannot be claimed simultaneously but in the instant case the plaintiffs did so. In this connection it may also be pointed out that the claim of title by adverse possession though accepted by the trial court was neither specifically pleaded nor proved by evidence. In the instant case and in the position like this the finding of title by adverse possession by the defendants as arrived by the trial court cannot but be treated as gratuitous finding of adverse possession and in this connection reference may be made to the case of Mahaprabhu Ram vs Gopal Ram Ram reported in 42 DLR (AD) 154. It may also pointed out that the learned Joint District Judge committed error of law without applying his judicial mind to the settled position of law that possession can never be adverse if it is referable to lawful title. Since in the instant case the defendants claim lawful title on the basis of two separate registered deed of patta, on the one hand, and title by adverse possession on the other, as such both the pleas taken by the out that the defendants took a duel plea in their pleading in a casual way, one is that they claim title on the basis of patta dated 26-9-40 and the other one for adverse possession. The learned Joint District Judge dismissed the suit and arrived at a conclusion that the defendants acquired title both on the basis of their pattas as well as by adverse possession, which is not sustainable in law, in view of the principle of law enunciated in 26 BLD (AD) 50 to the effect that case of title by adverse possession and a case of title on the basis of document cannot be claimed simultaneously but in the instant case the plaintiffs did so. In this connection it may also be pointed out that the claim of title by adverse possession though accepted by the trial court was neither specifically pleaded nor proved by evidence. In the instant case and in the position like this the finding of title by adverse possession by the defendants as arrived by the trial court cannot but be treated as gratuitous finding of adverse possession and in this connection reference may be made to the case of Mahaprabhu Ram vs Gopal Ram Ram reported in 42 DLR (AD) 154. It may also be pointed out that the learned Joint District Judge committed error of law without applying his judicial mind to the settled position of law that possession can never be adverse if it is referable to lawful title. Since in the instant case the defendants claim lawful title on the basis of two separate registered deed of patta, on the one hand and title by adverse possession on the other, as such both the pleas taken by the defendants must fail since in such a situation any court or tribunal becomes totally perplexed as to which version of their claim is to be believed or disbelieved. In this connection reference may be made to the case of Hazera Begum vs Rowshan Ara Begum reported in 39 DLR (AD) 22 and Mst Ghulam Hahi vs Muhammad Wanes Khan reported in 10 DLR (PC) 174. The learned Joint District Judge also failed lo appreciate that the defendants plea of adverse possession is not tenable in law against the plaintiffs since they are rightful claimants to the suit land. Reference may be made in this connection to the ease of Abdul Latif vs Abdul Malek Kazi reported in 1984 BLD (AD)15 = 38 DLR (AD) 2. It may also he pointed out that record prepared in the names of the defendants has got no presumptive value of correctness in as much as it has no basis particularly in view of our finding that Exhibit-Ga is not sustainable in law as such mere preparation of SA khatian in favour of the defendants or payment of rent by them to the Government do not create any title in their favour. In this connection reference may be made to the case Lal Miah being dead his heirs Momena Khatun vs Haji Md Ibrahim reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61. It may be pointed out further that the finding of the learned Joint District Judge on the point of resjudicata is patently wrong and not sustainable in law particularly in view of the settled principle that right to partition is a continuous right. Reference may made in this connection to the case of Mst Meheron Nessa vs Ali Ahmed Khan reported in 15 MLR 197 = 14 BLC 743 and in this connection it may be recalled that the finding of the learned Munsif, 3rd Court, Jessore in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 to the effect that the pattas in favour of both the mother and father of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 executed in the year 1940 and 1941 were bad in law, is a finding which has been subsisting till date particularly in view of the fact that the judgment of the said suit was not challenged before any higher forum at any stage and more so when the predecessors of the defendants 1 and 2 were very much contesting parties in that suit and in such view of the matter the said judgment is admissible in evidence in the instant suit and the same is binding upon the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 particularly in view of the provision of section 43 of the Evidence Act and in that view of the matter such finding with respect to the pattas of 1910 and 1941 operates as resjudicata in the instant case. In this connection reference may be made to the case of Nasim Ali vs Sakina Bibi reported in 1988 BLD 493. 

 41. The trial court ought to have held that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.21 of 1947 and Title Appeal No.98 of 1948 as also the judgment of Civil Revision Case No. 1190 of 1942 being not in the party those are not binding upon the plaintiffs and moreso judgment of a criminal proceeding cannot be admitted into evidence in deciding a civil suit and a contrary view being opposed to the settled principles of law those are not sustainable. 

 44. In view what has been stated above, we find substance in this appeal. Accordingly, the same is allowed without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-11-1993 passed by the Subordinate Judge now Joint District Judge, Jessore is hereby set-aside and Title Suit No. 6 of 1986 brought by the plaintiffs is hereby decreed as prayed for and the defendants are hereby directed to vacate the suit land upon removing the structures, if any, within 60 (sixty) days from the date of receipt of the judgment, failing which the plaintiffs are at liberty to recover khas, possession of the suit land through court by process of execution.

3. The case of the writ-petitioner as stated in the writ petition, inter-alia, was that he is a citizen of Bangladesh by birth and is also a citizen of Canada and resides there with his family. He purchased a plot measuring three kathas of land being Plot No. 19, at Road No. 22, Sector-14, Uttara Model Town, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as the plot in question) from original lessees, Khaliqur Rahman and Mohibur Rahman with permission of RAJUK dated 21-12-2006. The sale deed was executed and registered on 26-12-2006. The writ-petitioner received clearance certificate from RAJUK on 28-3-2007 for submitting plan. Accordingly, he submitted the plan with RAJUK on 23-5-2007 along with plan fee receipt dated 26-4-2007 under RAJUK File No. 3C-21/07. RAJUK did not take any step to approve the plan submitted almost two years back nor informed anything about such delay causing harassment to the writ-petitioner. The writ-petitioner, time to time, held conversations with RAJUK's authority and also met its Chairman who kept silent on the issue. Earlier RAJUK illegally issued Memo No. Rajuk /Estate 69(2) stha dated 23-7-2007 (Plot ID 14-22-19) to harass the writ-petitioner with malafide intention which was challenged in Writ Petition No. 58 of 2008. Upon hearing the parties, the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 31-7-2008 declared the said Memo without jurisdiction. The High Could Division held that: 

 11. The writ-petitioner also submitted a plan to RAJUK for construction of a 2 (two) storied building on the plot in question and RAJUK issued a clearance certificate on 28-3-2007 with the endorsement of writ-respondent No. 1 that the plan would be approved if submitted as per the Rules and also made site inspection to see whether ground work was done as per the plan which having been found no objection was made. On 28-6-2007, writ-respondent No. 4 in connivance with writ-respondent No. 1 made a false and frivolous allegation to RAJUK that his brother, writ-respondent No. 5, did not sell his portion of the plot in question to the writ-petitioner and that his brother did not execute any power of attorney in his favour and that the writ-petitioner obtained the power of attorney by forgery. On the basis of these wild and frivolous allegations (copy of which was not forwarded to the writ-petitioner), writ-respondent No. 1 most illegally issued Memo dated 23-7-2007 asking the writ-petitioner to stop the construction and to appear before him on 15-8-2007 for hearing over the title of the plot in question. The said letter dated 23-7-2007 was not, in fact, served upon the writ-petitioner for ill motive, he received the information from other source on phone and requested writ-respondent No. 1 to provide him an authenticated copy of the letter, although writ-respondent No. 1 supplied a photocopy thereof, he did not authenticate the same. On perusal of the letter, the writ-petitioner understood that writ-respondent No.4 in connivance with writ-respondent No. 1 made out a false case that his brother did not sell his portion of the plot in question to the writ-petitioner; that his brother did not execute the power of attorney and the writ-petitioner obtained the power of attorney by forgery. Writ-respondent No. 4 applied to RAJUK to accept the power of attorney of his brother and executed the sale deed on the basis of the said power of attorney, received full consideration of the plot in question being Taka 48,00,000 from the writ-petitioner and having not disputed his own transfer, could not dispute the transfer of his brother which was done by the same and one deed of sale. The allegation of writ-respondent No. 4 was totally malafide, frivolous and for unlawful gain, because the writ-petitioner resides in Canada with his family members. The writ-petitioner, however, came to Bangladesh and appeared before writ-respondent No. 1 with all documents, but writ-respondent No. 1 in spite of being 100% satisfied that the allegation of Khaliqur Rahman was totally false and baseless, failed to withdraw his stay order on construction and also failed to approve the plan which was submitted on 28-3-2007 as per the Rules. In fact, writ-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 had no basis to issue the Memo since they were not authorized in law to do so. This was a harassment of worst kind to a citizen who acquired the ownership of the plot in question through lawful means for valuable consideration. Writ-respondent No. 4 applied to RAJUK to approve the irrevocable power of attorney No. 21432 dated 17-12-2005 and RAJUK (respondent Nos. 1 and 2) approved the said power of attorney on the basis of which writ-respondent No. 4 executed and registered the deed of sale in favour of the writ-petitioner on receipt of full consideration, writ-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 acted illegally and without lawful authority in entertaining the frivolous complaint of writ-respondent No. 4 that his brother did not execute the said power of attorney. Although the writ-petitioner acquired title to the plot in question complying with all the formalities, writ-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 illegally withheld the approval of the plan submitted as per the Rules on 28-3-2007. The writ-respondents acted without lawful authority in failing to approve the plan within 9 (nine) months and in stopping the ground work towards construction on the basis of a complaint, which was totally false and baseless. Writ-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 were not the proper authorities to resolve such dispute. 

 18. Besides the explanations as to the delay in filing the leave petition, the leave petitioners have set out their own case stating, inter-alia, that RAJUK published an advertisement on 19-8-1995 in the "Dainik Bangla" inviting application from the owner of the land of LA Case No. 2 of 1987-88 for allotment of plot as affected person and accordingly, they made an application on 14-9-1995 to the RAJUK for getting lease of the plot of three kathas of land and deposited Taka 30,000. On consideration of the application, RAJUK by Memo No. RAJUK /Estate/ 289 dated 21-12-1996 allotted a plot of three kathas of land at Road No. 22 of Sector-14, Uttara, Dhaka at Taka 16,00,000 (Taka Sixteen Lakh) only per bigha. The leave petitioners paid the total amount of consideration for the plot in question by 5 (five) installments through Sonali Bank, RAJUK Branch, on obtaining money receipts as per terms and conditions of the RAJUK. Thereafter, leave petitioner No. 1 made an application for delivery of possession of the plot in question, but RAJUK refused to give delivery of possession on the ground that দুই ভাই এর সম্পত্তি একজনকে দেওয়া হবে না। Then leave petitioner No. 1 wrote his brother, leave petitioner No.2, for appointing him as attorney and accordingly, leave petitioner No. 2 constituted and appointed leave petitioner No. 1 as his attorney by executing a general power of attorney dated 16-8-2005 from UK as he was residing there. The power of attorney was duly attested by the officials of the High Commission of Bangladesh in London. Leave petitioner No. 1 on receipt of the power of attorney from his brother started process for authentication of the same by the Collector. Petitioner No. 1 came to Dhaka to make inquiry about the plot in question and visited the office of RAJUK and came to know that someone or other by means of forgery created a power of attorney in his name by forging the signature of his brother, leave petitioner No. 2 and in that power of attorney affixed the photo-graph of other person showing that to be the photograph of leave petitioner No. 1 and got that power of attorney approved by RAJUK and on the basis of that power of attorney got a deed of sale registered in favour of the writ-petitioner in respect of the plot in question and also got his name mutated collusively and obtained delivery of possession of the plot in question. Leave petitioner No. 1 on hearing about this fraudulent activities in respect of the plot in question made an application on 28-6-2007 to the Chairman, RAJUK for taking appropriate step to cancel the fraudulent transfer of the plot in question and to make arrangement for registration of the lease deed and delivery of possession of the lease hold plot in their favour. On receipt of the application dated 28-6-2007, the Director (Estate), RAJUK, respondent No. 2 herein, by the office letter vide Memo No. রাজউক/এষ্টেট/৬৯(৩)স্থাঃ তারিখ ২৩-৭-২০০৭,  requested the writ-petitioner to appear before him for hearing with original documents and papers on 15-8-2007 and also requested him to stop making of construction till disposal of the matter, copy of the said letter was sent to the leave petitioners. Pursuant to the said letter, the writ-petitioner appeared before respondent No.2 and attended the hearing. Leave petitioner No. 1 was present in the hearing which took place on 15-8-2007 and also on 21-8-2007, but RAJUK's authority did not give decision instantly. The writ-petitioner on 28-8-2007 wrote a letter to the Chairman, RAJUK stating his story acquiring the plot in question and also his appearance in the hearing dated 15-8-2007 and 21-8-2007 and prayed for early decision in this respect. Leave petitioner No. 1 on 5-9-2007 made another application with reference to the hearing which took place on 15-8-2007 and 21-8-2007 and submitted relevant papers including the power of attorney dated 16-8-2005 sent by his brother in his favour from UK. Leave petitioner No. 1 also submitted an email receipt from his brother wherein he clearly stated that he did not appoint anyone else as his attorney in order to sell the plot in question. The writ-petitioner appeared in the hearing dated 12-8-2007 followed by another hearing on 21-8-2007 and thus complied with the letter dated 23-7-2007 (impugned in the writ petition) and after such compliance, filed Writ Petition No. 58 of 2008 impugning the above letter dated 23-7-2007 and obtained the impugned judgment and order upon suppression of the facts and thus practised fraud upon the Court. After hearing and on scrutinizing the original documents, RAJUK by the decision taken in respect of item No. 58. 3 (ka) of the agenda of the meeting No. 6/2008 passed the following order 

 and informed the same to the writ-petitioner by letter dated 4-3-2009, copy of that decision was communicated to the leave petitioners. The leave petitioners on 3-5-2010 made an application to the Chairman, RAJUK for mutation of their names and delivery of possession of the plot in question to them and they on 28-10-2010 again made an application to RAJUK for allotting another plot to them in case the plot in question could not be given. "RAJUK lodged Motijheel Police Station Case No. 95 dated 31-10-2007 under sections 419, 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 34,109 of the Penal Code" and the police submitted charge-sheet against one Jahangir and others and the case is pending in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and the same is under trial. The registered power of attorney on the basis of which the transfer deed in favour of the writ-petitioner was registered, was allegedly executed on 7-12-2005 in Dhaka, Sylhet address of leave petitioner No. 2 was mentioned there though the plot in question is situated at Uttara, the power of attorney was registered in Gulshan Sub-Registrar's Office, as such, it is clear that the power of attorney was created and registered in the office of the Sub-Registrar having no jurisdiction. The executant of the power of attorney is a resident of UK and he had come to Bangladesh on 9-12-2004 and left for UK on 11-4-2005 and thereafter, he never came back to Bangladesh till date and, as such, the said registered power of attorney dated 7-12-2005 is forged and fabricated. The photograph affixed in the deed of transfer appears to be of some other person not of leave petitioner No. 1 and the mother's name of the leave petitioners given in the alleged transfer deed is different than the actual name of their mother and, as such, it is apparent that the registered power of attorney, the basis of the alleged deed of transfer, was forged, false, fabricated and illegal and by that transfer, the writ-petitioner did not acquire any right, title or interest whatsoever in the plot in question and he had no locus standi to file the writ petition. The writ-petitioner having attended the hearing as was requested by the letter impugned in the writ petition, had no locus standi to file the said writ petition and in spite of that filed the same by suppressing facts and obtained the impugned judgment and order without service of notice upon the leave petitioners knowing it fully well that he acquired no right in the plot in question and in that view of the matter, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set-aside. 

 21. From the writ petition, it appears that the writ-petitioner specifically stated therein that he purchased the plot in question from original lessees, Khaliqur Rahman and Mohibur Rahman (leave petitioners of CP No. 3033 of 2012) by registered deed of sale dated 26-12-2006 with due permission from RAJUK dated 21-12-2006, (with the writ petition the sale permission and the deed of sale were annexed as annexures-'B' and 'B(1)'; that after purchase, the writ-petitioner applied for mutation of his name with the record of RAJUK and RAJUK mutated his name which was confirmed by letter dated 6-2-2007; that the writ-petitioner decided to construct a three storied building for his family and accordingly applied to RAJUK in prescribed form upon which RAJUK issued its clearance certificate on 28-3-2007 with the endorsement that the plan will be approved if submitted as per the Rules and accordingly, he submitted the plan with RAJUK on 23-5-2007 along with plan fee receipt dated 26-4-2007 under RAJUK File No.3C-21/07, but RAJUK did not take any step to approve the plan; time to time, the writ-petitioner held conversation with RAJUK's authorities and also met its Chairman, but he kept silent on the issue and then on 30-3-2009 served demand justice notice asking them to do justice to him by approving the plan submitted almost 2(two) years before and to intimate compliance thereof within 7(seven) days of the notice, the notices were received by the writ-respondents, but they neither did anything nor responded to it. 

 23. In the writ petition, it was further stated that earlier, RAJUK illegally issued Memo No. RAJUK /Estate 69 (2) stha dated 23-7-2007 (plot No. ID 14-22-2009) to harass the writ-petitioner with malafide intention, which was challenged in Writ Petition No.58 of 2008 and a Division Bench of the High Court Division on hearing the Rule by the judgment and order dated 31-7-2008 declared the said Memo to have been issued without lawful authority and was of no legal effect. It was further stated that the writ-petitioner resides in Canada with his family and was compelled to come to Dhaka several times at huge cost and harassment for the matter. None of those assertions was either denied or disputed by the writ-respondent-petitioners herein by filing any affidavit-in-opposition. In the leave petition, those facts have not been denied as well. Thus, the claim of the writ-petitioner as to the acquisition of his title to the plot in question through purchase from the original lessees with due permission from RAJUK, mutation of his name with RAJUK and his possession therein and submission of the plan for the construction of the building as back as on 23-5-2007 remained unassailed. Therefore, the writ-respondents were under legal obligation to act as per the relevant Rules prevalent at the relevant time. And by no means, they could sit over the matter. 

 27. We also find the submission of Mr Mahbubey Alam that by giving direction to RAJUK and its officials to consider and approve the construction plan submitted by the writ-petitioner for approval, no chance was given to them to verify the "legality and proprietiness" of the deed and the other papers of the writ-petitioner, irrational as admittedly the writ-petitioner purchased the plot in question with the permission of RAJUK and he was delivered possession thereof, after purchase, RAJUK mutated his name and also gave clearance certificate to submit the plan for the construction of the building. Moreso, RAJUK got long two years’ time to verify the documents, the papers and the plan filed by the writ-petitioner, if it at all needed so. Further, when in Writ Petition No.58 of 2008, the letter dated 23-7-2007 issued by the Director (Estate) to the writ-petitioner by which he was asked to appear before him with the original deed and the other papers in support of his ownership, was declared to have been issued without lawful authority and was of no legal effect. 

 30. It is not disputed that RAJUK transferred the plot in question to writ-respondent Nos. 4 and 5, by way of a lease, for 99(ninety nine) years by a registered deed of agreement dated 21-12-2006; writ-respondent Nos.4 and 5 entered into an agreement with the writ-petitioner for sale of the plot in question at a fixed price of Taka 46,00,000 (it would be Taka 48,00,000, in the writ petition, the figure has been correctly mentioned) together with cost to be borne by the writ-petitioner; pursuant to such agreement, RAJUK accorded necessary permission to writ-respondent Nos. 4 and 5 to transfer the plot in question and on the basis of such permission, writ-respondent Nos. 4 and 5 transferred the plot in question to the writ-petitioner by a registered deed of sale dated 24-12-2006(the correct date is 26-12-2006 and in the writ petition the date has been correctly mentioned) and delivered possession thereof to him; with the approval of RAJUK, writ-respondent No.4 executed the deed of sale for himself and on behalf of writ-respondent No.5 on the basis of a registered power of attorney. Thus, being the owner in possession, the writ-petitioner got the plot in question mutated in his name with RAJUK and obtained necessary approval of a plan for the construction thereon; when the writ-petitioner had undertaken the construction work, he came to know about the existence of the impugned letter, copy of which was not sent to him. By the impugned letter, writ-respondent No. 1 asked the writ-petitioner to appear before him with the original deed and the other papers for hearing and determination of title in the plot in question. 

 31. The High Court Division observed that after transfer of the plot in question by way of lease for 99(ninety nine) years and further transfer and delivery of possession thereof by the lessees to the writ-petitioner, respondent No. 1 definitely knew that RAJUK had no right, title or possession or any interest therein. Neither writ-respondent No. 1 nor RAJUK had any authority or power to settle any question of title in any land in Bangladesh. When writ-respondent No. 1 issued the impugned letter, he was definitely actuated by certain ulterior motives, which was clear from the fact that he sent a copy of the letter to the Officer-in-Charge of Uttara Police Station, Dhaka for stopping the construction on the plot in question. Respondent No. 1 was definitely aware of the fact that he was not doing the right thing in writing the letter "What such letter could create any impact upon the petitioner, who is living in Canada, is easily understood." 

 32. In respect of CP No. 864 of 2010, Mr Mahbubey Alam has submitted that writ-respondent No. 1 on receipt of the complaint regarding title of the plot in question simply issued a letter on 23-7-2007 asking the writ-petitioner to appear before him on 15-8-2007 with the original documents for examination and till that date, request was made to post-pone the construction work, the writ-petitioner had no cause of action to file the writ petition. Moreso, RAJUK was quite authorized to ask any one claiming title to any of its leasehold plot to prove the ownership to such plot by producing document, in case any dispute is raised as to the title or ownership to such plot, the High Court Division, while making the Rule absolute, failed to consider these factual and legal aspects of the case. He has further submitted that the writ-petitioner was not authorized to construct the building on the plot in question inasmuch as he was merely issued a 'No objection certificate' upon his submission of plan for the construction of the building, but no order of approval of the plan was issued to him, but before approval of such plan, which is mandatorily required, started the construction works and, as such, the letter dated 23-7-2007 postponing the construction' was not illegal, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute declaring the impugned letter to have been issued without lawful authority and was of no legal effect. 

 33. Mr Tobarak Hossain, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners in CP No. 3033 of 2012, has tried to impress us by submitting that the writ-petitioner appeared at the hearing before writ-respondent No. 1 on 15-8-2007 followed by another hearing on 21-8-2007 and thus complied with the letter dated 23-7-2007 (impugned in the writ petition) and after such compliance, filed Writ Petition No. 58 of 2008 impugning the said letter and then obtained the impugned judgment and order upon suppression of facts and thus practised fraud upon the Court. He has submitted that the registered power of attorney, on the basis of which, the transfer of the plot in question was made in favour of the writ-petitioner, was allegedly executed on 7-12-2005 in Dhaka mentioning the address of executant- Mohibur Rahman (writ-respondent No. 5) at Sylhet though the plot in question situates at Uttara, clearly shows that the power of attorney was created and registered in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Gulshan having no jurisdiction. He has further submitted that the executant of the power of attorney is a resident of UK, who had come to Bangladesh on 9-12-2004 and left for UK on 11-4-2005; thereafter, he never came back to Bangladesh till date; it is apparent that the registered power of attorney, the basis of the alleged deed of transfer, was forged, false, fabricated and illegal and by that transfer, the writ-petitioner did not acquire any right, title or interest whatsoever in the plot in question and consequently he had no locus standi to file the writ petition challenging the impugned letter. He has further submitted that the notices of the Rule issued in the writ petition were not served upon writ-respondent Nos. 4 and 5 and thus they did not get any chance to contest the Rule and to place their case and could not point out the fact of forgery committed by the writ-petitioner in getting the registered deed of transfer in his favour in respect of the plot in question and as such, the matter may be sent back on remand to the High Court Division for hearing afresh giving them chance to place their case by setting aside the impugned judgment and order. 

 35. In the context, the pertinent question, that arises for consideration in these two CPs (864 of 2010 and 3033 of 2012), is whether writ-respondent No. 1 was legally authorized to issue the impugned letter dated 23-7-2006 to the writ-petitioner asking him to appear before him (writ-respondent No. 1 ) on 15-8-2007 with the original deed in respect of the plot in question and the other papers for attending a hearing to decide its true ownership and to stop all the construction works thereon till disposal of the matter. 

 41. Whether the power of attorney executed by writ-respondent No. 5 in favour of writ-respondent No.4 was the act of forgery, whether the deed of sale executed and registered by writ-respondent No.4 for self and on behalf of his brother (writ-respondent No.5) on the basis of the said power of attorney was valid or not; whether, by the sale deed dated 26-12-2006, the writ-petitioner acquired title to the plot in question and whether writ-respondent Nos. 4 and 5 transferred the plot in question to the writ-petitioner on receipt of valuable consideration of Taka 48,00,000 are the matters between writ-respondent Nos .4 and 5 and the writ-petitioner and such dispute or controversy cannot be decided by RAJUK. After the plot in question was transferred by the lessees to the writ-petitioner by a registered deed of sale with due permission from RAJUK, possession thereof was delivered to the transferee (the writ-petitioner) and his name was mutated with RAJUK, it lost all its grip on the question of ownership and it had no authority or locus standi to sit in an adjudication to decide the true ownership of the plot in question at the instance of writ-respondent Nos. 4 and 5 as was ventured by it by the impugned letter dated 23-7-2006. Therefore, the High Court Division rightly held that "After transfer of the land by way of lease for ninety nine years, and further transfer and delivery of possession of said land by the leasees(sic) to the petitioner, respondent No. 1 definitely know that RAJUK had no right, title or possession or any interest of such land. Neither respondent No. 1 nor RAJUK had any authority or power to settle any question of title in any land in Bangladesh." 

 44. By the decision as contained in the letter, in fact, RAJUK has sought to cancel the registered sale deed executed and registered by writ-respondent No.4 for himself and for writ-respondent No. 5 in favour of the writ-petitioner transferring the plot in question, as it is apparent from the letter that copy of the same was given to the Sub-Registrar Complex, Tejgaon and the Assistant Land Officer, Tahsil Office, Uttara, Dhaka. We wonder how RAJUK could take such a decision and under what legal authority. It is to be further noted that the letter dated 23-7-2007 impugned in Writ Petition No. 58 of 2008 was also issued at the instance of writ-respondent No. 4 on the complaint that the sale deed dated 26-12-2006 was obtained through forgery, but RAJUK chose not to contest the Rule issued in the writ petition and the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order (judgment was passed on 31-7-2008) declared the same to have been issued without lawful authority and was of no legal effect with the clear finding that "After transfer of the land by way of lease for ninety-nine years, and further transfer and delivery of possession of said land by the leases(sic) to the petitioner, respondent No. 1 definitely know that RAJUK had no right, title or possession or any interest in such land. Neither respondent No. 1 nor RAJUK had any authority or power to settle any question of title in any hand in Bangladesh." The action taken by RAJUK also appears to us outrageous inasmuch as they cancelled the mutation of the writ-petitioner's name after the letter dated 23-7-2007 issued by writ-respondent No. 1 was declared to have been issued without lawful authority and was of no legal effect by the High Court Division. We are compelled to make the above observations as we could not shut our eyes when such a disturbing fact was brought to our notice by the writ-respondents, i.e. the petitioners of both the CPs, though the letter dated 4-3-2009 is not the subject matter of the leave petitions.

full_judgment:
Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq , j :- The impugned order No.19 dated 19.08.1997 of the learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia passed in Title Suit No.102 of 1990 has been called in question by invoking the revisional jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court on laying a petition under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure whereupon a Single Judge of this Hon'ble Division on perusal of the same was placed to issue a rule calling upon the opposite party Nos.1-4 to show cause as to why the impugned order of the learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia passed in Title Suit No.102 of 1990 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 On 25.09.1990 the present petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.102 of 1990 in the Assistant Judge Court, Kumarkhali for declaration of title and confirmation of possession against the predecessor-in-interest of the opposite party Nos.1-4, Kulsum Nessa. 

 3. The specific case of the plaintiff in short is that the suit land originally belonged to Kulsum Nessa. Plaintiff is the brother's son of Kulsum Nessa. Kulsum Nessa was issueless. Kulsum Nessa transferred 39 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff by way of registered gift deed dated 20.01.1973 and delivered possession. Defendant threatened to dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land through other person as a result the plaintiff filed the suit. 

 5. After the death of Kulsum Nessa the present opposite party Nos.1-4 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.30 of 1994 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia against the present petitioner as defendant for setting aside the exparte decree dated 10.07.1991 passed in Title Suit No.102 of 1990. 

 6. The learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia was pleased to decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 26.02.1995 in Title Suit No.30 of 1994. 

 7. Against the judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali the present petitioner as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.43 of 1995 in the Court of District Judge, Kushtia, the same was heard by the learned subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Kushtia and was pleased to disallow the appeal by her judgment and decree dated 26.04.1997. 

 8. After disposal of appeal the plaintiff of Title Suit No.102 of 1990 filed an application on 04.08.1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali for starting the proceeding of Title Suit No.102 of 1990. But the learned Court did not pass any order on the application of the plaintiff dated 04.08.1997. 

 9. The plaintiff-petitioner filed another verified application dated 19.08.1997 for calling the records of Title Suit No.102 of 1990 and praying for hearing along with the earlier application dated 04.08.1997. 

 11. Mr. Md. Saidul Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that once an application is filed by any party the Court must dispose of the same on merit. He further submits that there are 4 remedies against the exparte decree (1) A Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the original Suit. (2) An appeal to the higher Court under Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, (3) A review under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and (4) a separate suit for setting aside the exparte decree. In that view of the matter the learned Assistant Judge committed a serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner further submits that the impugned order dated 19.08.1997 is a non speaking order and is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the impugned order is self contradictory the reason is that he himself stated that the application is unlawful but no explanation is given as to why it is unlawful while passing the impugned order he simply kept the application in the records of the suit. The learned Judge feel into gross error in not passing any order on the application and thus the impugned order suffers from serious miscarriage of justice resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the impugned order is a non speaking order. He also submits that the impugned order is not a proper order and thus deserves interference under the provision of law as contained in Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention he refers to the case of Jahura Bibi and others -Vs- Mvi. Habibur Rahman and other reported in 15 BLD (AD) 519 where their lordships held that ; 

 14. On consideration of the submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and on perusal of the citation as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of his contention I find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The impugned order passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge-in-charge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia dated 19.8.1997 in Title Suit No.102 of 1990 is absolutely a non speaking order and in my view it is no order in the eye of law and the same deserves interference under the Revisional jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Assistant Judge without disposing of the application on merit cannot keep the matter pending for an indefinite period by simply observing `শুনিলাম। প্রার্থনা আইন সম্মত নহে। দরখাস্তটি নথিভূক্ত হউক।' This sort of order is ex-facie illegal, misconceived order and also no order in the eye of law. The learned Assistant Judge in passing the impugned order committed  serious illegality and miscarriage of justice which deserves interference under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same is liable to be set aside. In that view of the matter the impugned order dated 19.8.1997 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge-in-charge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia in Title Suit No.102 of 1990 is hereby set aside. 

 16. The learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkahli, Kushtia is hereby directed to restore the Title Suit No.102 of 1990 to its original file and number after vacating the exparte order and proceed with the trial of Title Suit No.102 of 1990 in accordance with law.
